claims.statement: Keibu Keioiba is a tiger-headed, human-bodied creature of Meitei mythology and folklore in Manipur.
claims.statement_id: Keibu Keioiba adalah makhluk berkepala harimau dan bertubuh manusia dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di Manipur.
claims.quote: Keibu Keioiba, also known as Kabui Keioiba, is a mythical creature with the head of a tiger and the body of a human in the Meitei mythology and folklore of Manipur. According to legend, he was once a skilful priest named Kabui Salang Maiba. He used witchcraft to turn himself into a ferocious tiger. As punishment of his pride, he could not completely turn back to his original human form.

claims.statement: Legend describes him as the priest Kabui Salang Maiba who used witchcraft to become a tiger.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ia dahulu pendeta Kabui Salang Maiba yang menggunakan sihir untuk berubah menjadi harimau.
claims.quote: According to legend, he was once a skilful priest named Kabui Salang Maiba. He used witchcraft to turn himself into a ferocious tiger.

claims.statement: In the tale an old woman directs the creature to Thabaton, who is home alone.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisahnya, seorang perempuan tua mengarahkan makhluk itu kepada Thabaton yang tinggal sendirian.
claims.quote: Keibu Keioiba was a human in the daytime and a tiger at night. During night, he prowled around looking for food. One night, he found an older woman's house and planned to devour her. The old woman said that her wrinkled skin would not be tasty and suggested that he eat a beautiful and young woman named Thabaton instead. Thabaton was the only sister in a family with seven brothers.

claims.statement: He takes Thabaton to the forest and forces her to become his wife.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa Thabaton ke hutan dan memaksanya menjadi istrinya.
claims.quote: Keibu Keioiba has not eaten Thabaton. Instead, he has forced Thabaton to become his wife, and they live together in the forest.

claims.statement: Thabaton sends him to fetch water with a pipe open at both ends so she can escape with her brothers.
claims.statement_id: Thabaton menyuruhnya mengambil air dengan pipa terbuka di kedua ujung agar dapat melarikan diri bersama saudara-saudaranya.
claims.quote: Thabaton gives him a hollow utong (bamboo pipe) open at both ends. She tells Keibu Keioiba to fetch water from the stream with the utong.

claims.statement: In the translation of Jayantakumar Sharma's tale Keibu Keioiba is human by day and a tiger at night.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan cerita Jayantakumar Sharma, Keibu Keioiba menjadi manusia pada siang hari dan harimau pada malam hari.
claims.quote: there lived a man called Keibu Keioiba who was human in daytime and during night he would turn into a tiger.

claims.statement: Macchanu is Hanuman's son in the Thai and other versions of the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Macchanu adalah putra Hanuman dalam versi Thailand dan versi lain Ramayana.
claims.quote:
Macchanu (Thai: มัจฉานุ; RTGS: Matchanu; Khmer: មច្ឆានុប; RTGS: Macchanub) is the son of Hanuman that appears in the 
Thai version of the story and other versions of the Ramayana.

claims.statement: He is described as having a vanara upper body and a fish tail.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan bertubuh atas vanara dan berekor ikan.
claims.quote: who looked like vanara from waist-up but had tail of a fish.

claims.statement: Akashvani reveals that the enemy Hanuman is about to harm is his own son by Suvannamaccha.
claims.statement_id: Suara Akashvani mengungkapkan bahwa musuh yang hendak diserang Hanuman adalah putranya dari Suvannamaccha.
claims.quote: reveals by way of Akashvani that the enemy, whom he is going to harm is his own son born by his union with Suvannamaccha, the mermaid daughter of Ravana.

claims.statement: In another version he guards a pond on Hanuman's journey to find Rama and Laxmana.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain, ia menjaga kolam pada perjalanan Hanuman mencari Rama dan Laxmana.
claims.quote: while following Maiyarap in order to find Rama and Laxmana, who have been abducted by Maiyarap and taken to his kingdom in netherworld, Hanuman reaches a pond, where he encounters Macchanu.

claims.statement: He names Maiyarap as his foster father and gives a riddle about the entrance through a lotus.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyebut Maiyarap sebagai ayah angkat, lalu memberi petunjuk teka-teki tentang jalan masuk melalui teratai.
claims.quote: He tells Hanuman that Maiyarap is his foster father, ... tells Hanuman through a riddle the entrance to the netherworld lies inside the lotus in the pond he was guarding.

claims.statement: Thailand Foundation describes Macchanu as raised by Maiyarap and assigned to guard the netherworld entrance.
claims.statement_id: Thailand Foundation menyebut Macchanu dibesarkan Maiyarap dan ditugaskan menjaga jalan masuk dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Macchanu was raised by Maiyarap (Ahiravan), the demon king of the netherworld, and tasked with guarding its entrance.

claims.statement: Mahishi is a demoness in Hindu mythology whose story concerns Ayyappa and Sabarimala.
claims.statement_id: Mahishi adalah sosok iblis perempuan dalam mitologi Hindu yang kisahnya berkaitan dengan Ayyappa dan Sabarimala.
claims.quote: In Hindu mythology, Mahishi is a powerful demoness whose narrative is central to the origin of Lord Ayyappa and the traditions of the Sabarimala temple. She was the sister of the buffalo-demon Mahishasura.

claims.statement: This source calls her the sister of the buffalo demon Mahishasura.
claims.statement_id: Sumber ini menyebutnya saudari Mahishasura, iblis berwujud kerbau.
claims.quote: In Hindu mythology, Mahishi is a powerful demoness whose narrative is central to the origin of Lord Ayyappa and the traditions of the Sabarimala temple. She was the sister of the buffalo-demon Mahishasura.

claims.statement: She receives a boon that only a child of Shiva and Vishnu's union can kill her.
claims.statement_id: Ia menerima anugerah bahwa hanya anak dari persatuan Shiva dan Vishnu yang dapat membunuhnya.
claims.quote: From Brahma, she secured a specific boon: that she could only be slain by a child born of the union of Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu. Believing such a birth to be biologically impossible, she unleashed a reign of terror, conquering the Svarga and ousting Indra from his throne.

claims.statement: Ayyappan's birth satisfies that condition through Shiva's union with Mohini, Vishnu's female manifestation.
claims.statement_id: Kisah kelahiran Ayyappan menjawab syarat anugerah itu melalui persatuan Shiva dengan Mohini, penjelmaan perempuan Vishnu.
claims.quote: To counter Mahishi's invincibility, the deities sought a solution. Following the Samudra Manthana , Shiva was captivated by the beauty of Mohini, the female avatar of Vishnu. Their union led to the birth of Ayyappan (also known as Manikandan or Dharma Sastha), the divine child born of two male deities, thereby fulfilling the technical requirements of Mahishi’s boon.

claims.statement: Ayyappan seizes her horns and casts her to Earth during their battle.
claims.statement_id: Ayyappan menangkap tanduknya dan menjatuhkannya ke bumi dalam pertarungan.
claims.quote: When Mahishi attempted to storm heaven once more, Ayyappan, then a young prince, ascended to the celestial realms. He engaged the demoness in a fierce battle, eventually catching her by her horns and hurling her down to Earth. She landed on the banks of the Azhuthayar River near Sabarimala, where Ayyappan performed a divine dance on her body as she died.

claims.statement: Kerala Tourism explains Ayyappa's birth mission as eliminating the threat posed by Mahishi.
claims.statement_id: Kerala Tourism menjelaskan bahwa misi kelahiran Ayyappa adalah menghapus ancaman Mahishi.
claims.quote: The birth mission of Ayyappa was to eliminate the threat caused by Mahishi, a demoness.

claims.statement: Dragons feature in Meitei stories, literature, mythology and religion in Manipur.
claims.statement_id: Naga memiliki peran dalam cerita, sastra, mitologi, dan agama Meitei di Manipur.
claims.quote: Dragons play a significant role in the legendary accounts of Meitei folklore, literature, mythology and religion of ancient, medieval and modern Manipur.

claims.statement: The source says historical records have given Pakhangba a credulous halo as the God-king of Manipur.
claims.statement_id: Sumber ini menyebut bahwa catatan sejarah memberi 'lingkar kemuliaan' yang dipercaya untuk memuliakan Pakhangba sebagai raja-dewa Manipur.
claims.quote: historical records have rendered a credulous halo to glorify Pakhangba as a God-king of Manipur

claims.statement: Because of his divine power to move about at night as a dragon, he is also known as Sanahing Pakhangba.
claims.statement_id: Karena kekuatan ilahinya untuk bergerak pada malam hari sebagai naga, ia juga dikenal sebagai Sanahing Pakhangba.
claims.quote: Because of his divine power to be able to move about at night as dragon he is also known as Sanahing Pakhangba.

claims.statement: Manipur's kings use the dragon image as royal insignia.
claims.statement_id: Raja-raja Manipur menggunakan citra naga sebagai lambang kerajaan.
claims.quote: And all Rajas of Manipur have since used the dragon ... to represent the royal insignia.

claims.statement: Kangla Sha is a guardian dragon lion that safeguards the Kangla Palace and is usually depicted in pairs.
claims.statement_id: Kangla Sha adalah naga-singa penjaga yang melindungi Istana Kangla dan biasanya digambarkan berpasangan.
claims.quote: Kangla Sha is the Guardian dragon lion, safeguarding the Kangla Palace. Kangla Sha are usually depicted in pairs.

claims.statement: Pakhangba is the youngest son of the supreme mother earth goddess Leimarel Sidabi; his father Atingkok gave him the throne of the universe to protect and rule the world, and he could change himself into both a serpentine dragon and a human.
claims.statement_id: Pakhangba adalah putra bungsu Leimarel Sidabi, dewi ibu bumi tertinggi; ayahnya Atingkok memberinya takhta alam semesta untuk melindungi dan memerintah dunia, dan ia dapat mengubah dirinya menjadi naga berbentuk ular maupun manusia.
claims.quote: Pakhangba is the youngest son of Leimarel Sidabi, the supreme mother earth goddess. He was given the throne of the universe to protect and rule the world by Atingkok, his father. He could change himself into both a serpentine dragon and a human.

claims.statement: Nongshaba, the dragon lion, is a child of Atingkok, the Supreme Being; unlike his siblings he always remains in the form of the mythical beast rather than that of a God (human figure).
claims.statement_id: Nongshaba, sang naga-singa, adalah anak Atingkok, Sang Maha Tinggi; berbeda dari saudara-saudaranya, ia selalu tetap berwujud makhluk mitos, bukan wujud dewa (manusia).
claims.quote: Nongshaba, the dragon lion, is a child of Atingkok, the Supreme Being. Unlike his siblings, he always remains in the form of the mythical beast rather than that of a God (human figure).

claims.statement: Poubi Lai is the tyrant dragon serpent of the primitive Loktak Lake, a popular figure in Meitei folklore and mythology.
claims.statement_id: Poubi Lai adalah naga-ular tiran dari Danau Loktak purba dan tokoh populer dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Meitei.
claims.quote: Poubi Lai is the tyrant dragon serpent of the primitive Loktak Lake. This huge dragon is a popular figure in Meitei folklore and mythology.

claims.statement: Taoroinai is a mythical dragon serpent that lives in the cosmic ocean and is known for bringing the divine celestial egg (nonglum) down to earth.
claims.statement_id: Taoroinai adalah naga-ular mitos yang hidup di samudra kosmik dan dikenal karena menurunkan telur langit ilahi (nonglum) ke bumi.
claims.quote: Taoroinai (Old Manipuri: Taoloinai) is a mythical dragon serpent, who lives in the cosmic ocean. It is known for bringing down the divine celestial egg (nonglum) down to earth.

claims.statement: The Hiyang Hiren is a well-furnished race boat, often built in the shape of a dragon, and many legends say it possesses spiritual powers.
claims.statement_id: Hiyang Hiren adalah perahu pacu yang dihias lengkap, sering dibuat berbentuk naga, dan banyak legenda menyebutnya memiliki kekuatan spiritual.
claims.quote: The Hiyang Hiren (Old Manipuri: Hiyang Hilen) is a well furnished race boat. This is often built in the shape of a dragon. Many legends say that it possesses spiritual powers.

claims.statement: According to this source, legends have grown up around Pakhangba declaring that he had the power of changing his shape into that of a snake.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber ini, di sekitar tokoh Pakhangba tumbuh legenda yang menyatakan ia memiliki kekuatan mengubah wujudnya menjadi ular.
claims.quote: Around the personage of Pakhangba legends have grown up which declare him to have had the power of changing his shape into that of a snake

claims.statement: According to this source, Pakhangba, ancestor of the Ningthaja clan, is believed to still sometimes appear to men in the form of a snake.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber ini, Pakhangba, leluhur klan Ningthaja, dipercaya masih kadang menampakkan diri kepada manusia dalam wujud ular.
claims.quote: In the case of the ancestor of the Ningthaja clan, Pakhangba, we have the curious superstition that he still sometimes appears to men, but in the form of a snake

claims.statement: In an older account quoted in this source, the snake sometimes appears of great size, taken as a sign of displeasure, while a diminutive form is a sign that it is in good humour.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan catatan lama di sumber ini, ular itu kadang tampak sangat besar, yang dianggap tanda ia tidak senang; selama tetap kecil, itu tanda suasana hatinya baik.
claims.quote: This snake appears, they say, sometimes of great size, and when he does so it is indicative of his being displeased with something. But as long as he remains of diminutive form it is a sign that he is in good humour.

claims.statement: In an older account quoted in this source, the Raja's peculiar god is a species of snake called Pakung-ba from which the royal family claims descent; when it appears the priestess coaxes it onto a cushion and performs ceremonies to please it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan catatan lama di sumber ini, dewa khusus raja adalah sejenis ular bernama Pakung-ba yang diklaim sebagai leluhur keluarga kerajaan; saat muncul, ia dibujuk naik ke bantal oleh pendeta perempuan yang melakukan upacara untuk menyenangkannya.
claims.quote: The Raja’s peculiar god is a species of snake called Pakung-ba, from which the Royal family claims descent. When it appears it is coaxed on to a cushion by the priestess in attendance, who then performs certain ceremonies to please it.

claims.statement: According to this source, the place of execution was in front of the stone Dragons (the Nongsha), which stood before the Kangla or Coronation Hall, or under a tree on the bank of the Nambol river.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber ini, tempat eksekusi ialah di depan naga-naga batu (Nongsha) yang berdiri di depan Kangla atau Balai Penobatan, atau di bawah pohon di tepi sungai Nambol.
claims.quote: The place of execution was either in front of the stone Dragons (the Nongsha), which stood before the Kangla or Coronation Hall, or under a tree on the bank of the Nambol river.

claims.statement: According to this source, Kangla-Sha (twin-horned dragon) used to be a myth-associated icon of Manipur's kings, and its sculptured statues at the entrance of the royal palace were a place of pride for all royal ceremonies.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber ini, Kangla-Sha (naga bertanduk dua) dahulu menjadi lambang yang dikaitkan dengan mitos para raja Manipur; patung-patungnya di pintu masuk istana kerajaan menjadi tempat kehormatan bagi semua upacara kerajaan.
claims.quote: Yet another myth-associated icon of Manipur kings used to be Kangla-Sha (twin-horned dragon as shown in an actual photograph published in T.C.Hodson's The Meitheis (1908) (Photoplate:2-4) whose sculptured statues at the entrance of the royal Palace (UTTARA) used to be the place of pride (holiest of holy) for all royal ceremonies

claims.statement: Munjya are ghosts of boys who, in Maharashtra and Konkan folklore, died after the sacred-thread ceremony but before marriage.
claims.statement_id: Munjya adalah hantu anak laki-laki yang menurut cerita rakyat Maharashtra dan pesisir Konkan meninggal setelah upacara benang suci tetapi sebelum menikah.
claims.quote: According to folklore in Maharashtra and the Konkan coast, Munjya is believed to be the ghosts of boys who died after this ceremony but before marriage, inhabiting peepal trees.

claims.statement: They are believed to inhabit peepal trees.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dipercaya menghuni pohon peepal.
claims.quote: Munjya is believed to be the ghosts of boys who died after this ceremony but before marriage, inhabiting peepal trees.

claims.statement: Some tales describe restless bachelor ghosts with cleverness and multilingual abilities.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian cerita menggambarkan hantu bujang yang gelisah, cerdik, dan menguasai beberapa bahasa.
claims.quote: Munjya's are described as restless bachelor ghosts who roam trees at night, possessing cleverness and multilingual abilities.

claims.statement: Although usually harmless, they may retaliate against people who defile their tree homes.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun umumnya tidak berbahaya, mereka dapat membalas orang yang mengotori pohon tempat tinggalnya.
claims.quote: While most Munjya's are not harmful, they may retaliate against those who defile their tree homes, potentially pelting offenders with stones or causing accidents.

claims.statement: Some tales describe stone throwing or accidents as retaliation.
claims.statement_id: Cerita tertentu menyebut pelemparan batu atau kecelakaan sebagai bentuk pembalasan.
claims.quote: While most Munjya's are not harmful, they may retaliate against those who defile their tree homes, potentially pelting offenders with stones or causing accidents.

claims.statement: The filmmakers adapt Konkan coastal folklore into the horror comedy Munjya.
claims.statement_id: Para pembuat film mengadaptasi cerita rakyat pesisir Konkan menjadi komedi horor Munjya.
claims.quote: Writer Niren Bhatt and director-writer Amar Kaushik, who made Stree 2 and Bhediya, decided to fashion a folklore into a classic horror comedy—a medium they ace. And thus, Munjya came into being.

claims.statement: Poubi Lai is a dragon python of Meitei mythology and folklore dwelling in Manipur's Loktak Lake.
claims.statement_id: Poubi Lai adalah naga piton dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei yang menghuni Danau Loktak di Manipur.
claims.quote: Poubi Lai was an ancient dragon python, who dwelled in the Loktak Lake of Manipur, in Meitei mythology and folklore. It is also referred to as "Loch Ness Monster of Manipur".

claims.statement: In one tale fishing by Moirang's fishermen angers it and it threatens the kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, ia marah akibat kegiatan nelayan Moirang dan mengancam kerajaan.
claims.quote: In the Loktak lake, the spirit of Poubi Lai was awakened by the fishing activities of the fishermen of Moirang. Being angered, Poubi Lai destroyed many human habitats and killed many people.

claims.statement: It demands a basket of rice and a human each day from Moirang's king.
claims.statement_id: Ia menuntut satu keranjang beras dan satu manusia setiap hari dari raja Moirang.
claims.quote: He threatened the King of Ancient Moirang to offer him one Shangbai (basket) of rice and one human every day.

claims.statement: Another version locates it at Karang Hill and describes it preying on fishermen.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain menempatkannya di Karang Hill dan menggambarkannya memangsa nelayan.
claims.quote: In another version of the story, Poubi Lai (Paobirai) lives in the isle of the Karang Hill in the Loktak lake. It hunted the fishermen of Moirang coming to the lake and devoured them. It even attacked human settlement and hunted for its prey.

claims.statement: The source records Poubi Lai in the Meitei manuscript Khongul Lirakpa.
claims.statement_id: Sumber menyebut Poubi Lai dalam naskah Meitei Khongul Lirakpa.
claims.quote: Poubi Lai (Paobirai) is mentioned in the ancient Meitei manuscript called the "Khongul Lirakpa".

claims.statement: When it was a young man's turn, he sought help from Kabui Salang Maiba (or 'Kabui Tomba'), a shaman priest king of the Kabui tribe in the Salangthel hill range of Loktak Lake, who promised to save the kingdom from the gigantic evil creature.
claims.statement_id: Ketika giliran seorang pemuda tiba, ia meminta pertolongan Kabui Salang Maiba (atau 'Kabui Tomba'), seorang maiba (dukun-pendeta) sekaligus raja suku Kabui di pegunungan Salangthel di Danau Loktak, yang berjanji menyelamatkan kerajaan dari makhluk raksasa jahat itu.
claims.quote: When it was the turn of a young man, the lad sought help from Kabui Salang Maiba (or "Kabui Tomba"). The maiba was a shaman priest king of Kabui tribe in the Salangthel hill range of the Loktak lake. He promised to save the kingdom from the gigantic evil creature.

claims.statement: The maiba transformed a Tou plant (an aquatic plant), or a Khok Waa bamboo plant in another version, into a powerful 'Long' (a 9-pointed javelin), and later slew Poubi Lai with that deadly weapon.
claims.statement_id: Sang maiba mengubah tanaman Tou (tanaman air), atau bambu Khok Waa dalam versi lain, menjadi 'Long' yang ampuh (lembing bermata sembilan), lalu membunuh Poubi Lai dengan senjata mematikan itu.
claims.quote: He transformed a Tou plant (an aquatic plant) (or a Khok Waa bamboo plant in another version) into a powerful "Long" (a 9 pointed javelin). Later, the maiba slayed Poubi Lai with the deadly weapon.

claims.statement: In 2002 the wood-carver Karam Dineshwar Singh conceived and chiselled a 21-foot-long artwork which found expression from a dream he had of Poubi Lai one night.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2002, pemahat kayu Karam Dineshwar Singh mewujudkan karya sepanjang 21 kaki yang bermula dari mimpinya tentang Poubi Lai pada suatu malam.
claims.quote: Conceived and chiseled by (late) wood-carver Karam Dineshwar Singh, who was one of the successors of the royal family-associated Karigar craftspeople, the 21-foot-long artwork found expression in 2002 from a dream he had of Poubi Lai one night.

claims.statement: The sculpture was completed in six months and had its inaugural exhibition the same year at the Manipur State Museum in Imphal, according to museum sources.
claims.statement_id: Patung itu selesai dalam enam bulan dan pameran perdananya diadakan pada tahun yang sama di Museum Negara Bagian Manipur di Imphal, menurut sumber museum.
claims.quote: Completed in six months, the sculpture had its inaugural exhibition the same year at Manipur State Museum in Imphal, Museum sources said.

claims.statement: According to art historians, this sculpture was the first of its kind to draw a large audience to watch live presentations of Poubi Lai, previously heard of only in stories; the work has also travelled to France for an exhibition.
claims.statement_id: Menurut para sejarawan seni, patung ini yang pertama jenisnya yang menarik perhatian khalayak luas untuk menyaksikan penampilan langsung Poubi Lai yang sebelumnya hanya didengar dalam cerita; karya ini juga pernah dibawa ke Prancis untuk pameran.
claims.quote: Art historians note that this sculpture was the first of its kind to draw the attention of a large audience and watch the live presentations of Poubi Lai about which they have ever heard only in stories. The work has travelled to France for an exhibition.

claims.statement: On 21 July 2015 a single-object exhibition entitled 'Poubi Lai-The story of a giant python' was inaugurated at the National Museum in New Delhi.
claims.statement_id: Pada 21 Juli 2015, sebuah pameran satu objek berjudul 'Poubi Lai-The story of a giant python' diresmikan di Museum Nasional, New Delhi.
claims.quote: New Delhi, July 21 2015 : The Additional Secretary of Ministry of Culture, KK Mittal today inaugurated the single object exhibition entitled 'Poubi Lai-The story of a giant python' at the National Museum here.

claims.statement: The buru or bura is an aquatic cryptic animal featured in a foundation myth of the Apatani people.
claims.statement_id: Buru atau bura adalah hewan kriptik akuatik yang muncul dalam mitos asal-usul masyarakat Apatani.
claims.quote: The buru or bura is an aquatic cryptic animal featured in a foundation myth of the Apatani people.

claims.statement: Stories of the Apatani migration to the Ziro Valley in Arunachal Pradesh tell of a swamp occupying the valley, inhabited by fierce, crocodile-like creatures.
claims.statement_id: Kisah migrasi masyarakat Apatani ke Lembah Ziro di Arunachal Pradesh menceritakan rawa yang menempati lembah itu dan dihuni makhluk-makhluk ganas mirip buaya.
claims.quote: Stories of the migration of the Apatani to their present location in the Ziro Valley of Arunachal Pradesh tell of a swamp occupying the valley, inhabited by fierce, crocodile-like creatures.

claims.statement: Mills and Stonor collected buru accounts from Apatani people in 1945 and 1946.
claims.statement_id: Mills dan Stonor mengumpulkan cerita tentang buru dari masyarakat Apatani pada 1945 dan 1946.
claims.quote: In 1945 and 1946, James Philip Mills and Charles Stonor gathered details about the buru from the Apatani people. According to the Apatani elders, when their forefathers migrated to Ziro Valley, the valley was primarily a marsh which was populated by burus. The Apatani people decided to settle in the valley because of its fertility and good climate.

claims.statement: Apatani elders recount that draining the wetlands killed most burus while some went underground into springs.
claims.statement_id: Tetua Apatani menuturkan bahwa pengeringan rawa menghilangkan sebagian besar buru, sementara sebagian masuk ke mata air bawah tanah.
claims.quote: The burus were ostensibly eliminated when the Apatani people drained the wetlands to facilitate rice cultivation. Most of the burus died because of the drainage, and many supposedly went underground into the springs.

claims.statement: According to the abstract of this study, the buru is a mythical figure, a kind of animal-chimaera, that plays a key role in the myth of the origins of the Apatani.
claims.statement_id: Menurut abstrak kajian ini, buru adalah tokoh mitos berupa semacam hewan-kimera yang berperan kunci dalam mitos asal-usul masyarakat Apatani.
claims.quote: the study aims to explain the symbolisms and functions inherent in the mythical figure of the buru, a kind of animal-chimaera, which plays a key role in the myth of the origins of the Apatani.

claims.statement: According to the abstract, the misinterpretation of the British expedition in the 1950s gave rise to beliefs that today (mostly in the West) aim to prove the real existence of the buru, extrapolating it from the folklore record.
claims.statement_id: Menurut abstrak kajian ini, salah tafsir atas ekspedisi Inggris pada 1950-an melahirkan sejumlah keyakinan yang di zaman sekarang (kebanyakan di Barat) berusaha membuktikan keberadaan nyata buru dengan mencabutnya dari catatan cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: The misinterpretation of the British expedition in the 1950s gave rise to a series of beliefs that in contemporary times (mostly in the West) have aimed to prove the real existence of the buru, extrapolating it from the folklore record.

claims.statement: According to the abstract, for this reason the buru has today become a sort of post-modern legend, or better a classical figure of cryptozoology, understood as pseudoscience and a sub-cultural product.

claims.statement: Hatsadiling is a mythical bird commonly found in Northern Thai art.

The creature is considered to be the size of a house, with the head and body of a lion, trunk and tusks of an elephant, the comb of a cock, and the wings of a bird.

claims.statement: Ichchhadhari Nag are shapeshifting cobras of Indian folklore and mythology.
claims.statement_id: Ichchhadhari Nag adalah ular kobra pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi India.
claims.quote: ಇಚ್ಛಧಾರಿ ನಾಗ್ (ಸ್ತ್ರೀಲಿಂಗ: ಇಚ್ಛಧಾರಿ ನಾಗಿನ್) ಭಾರತೀಯ ಜಾನಪದ ಮತ್ತು ಪೌರಾಣಿಕೆ ಕಥೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬರುವ ಆಕಾರವನ್ನು ಬದಲಾಯಿಸುವ ನಾಗರಹಾವುಗಳಾಗಿವೆ.

claims.statement: There are stories that they can change from a snake into human form and back into a snake; they are described as great devotees of Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Ada kisah bahwa mereka dapat berubah dari ular menjadi rupa manusia dan kembali menjadi ular; mereka disebut pemuja besar Shiva.
claims.quote: ಇವುಗಳು ಹಾವಿನಿಂದ ಮನುಷ್ಯರೂಪಕ್ಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮನುಷ್ಯರೂಪದಿಂದ ಪುನಃ ಹಾವಾಗುವ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೊಂದಿವೆ ಎಂಬ ಕಥೆಗಳಿವೆ. ಅವರು ಶಿವನ ಮಹಾನ್ ಭಕ್ತರಾಗಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

claims.statement: They are believed to gain human form after Shiva's blessing.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dipercaya memperoleh wujud manusia setelah mendapat berkat Shiva.
claims.quote: ಶಿವನಿಂದ ಆಶೀರ್ವದಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟ ನಂತರ ಅವರು ತಮ್ಮದೇ ಆದ ಮಾನವ ರೂಪವನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.

claims.statement: Ichchhadhari nags and nagins have a jewel called the nagamani, said to be more valuable than any precious stone because it can bring its owner back to life and grant immense power.
claims.statement_id: Ichchhadhari nag dan nagin memiliki permata bernama nagamani, yang lebih berharga daripada batu mulia mana pun karena dapat menghidupkan kembali pemiliknya dan memberi kekuatan yang sangat besar.
claims.quote: ಇಚ್ಛಧಾರಿ ನಾಗಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ನಾಗಿಣಿಯರು ನಾಗಮಣಿ ಎಂಬ ಆಭರಣವನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಇವು ಯಾವುದೇ ಅಮೂಲ್ಯವಾದ ಕಲ್ಲುಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಮೌಲ್ಯಯುತವಾಗಿದೆ. ಏಕೆಂದರೆ ಅದು ತನ್ನ ಮಾಲೀಕರನ್ನು ಮತ್ತೆ ಬದುಕಿಸುವ ಮತ್ತು ಅಪಾರವಾದ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ನೀಡುವ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿದೆ.

claims.statement: The pungi instrument's sound is believed to make them lose control and reveal their true form.
claims.statement_id: Bunyi alat pungi dipercaya membuat mereka kehilangan kendali dan menampakkan wujud asli.
claims.quote: ಸಪೇರಾ (ಸ್ನೇಕ್ ಚಾರ್ಮರ್) ಅಥವಾ ಹಾವಾಡಿಗ ಬಳಸುವ ಗಾಳಿ ವಾದ್ಯವಾದ ಪುಂಗಿಯ ಶಬ್ದವನ್ನು ಕೇಳಿದಾಗ ನಾಗ್ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ನಾಗಿನ್ನರು/ನಾಗಿಣಿಯರು ತಮ್ಮ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣವನ್ನು ಕಳೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ ಮತ್ತು ತಮ್ಮ ನಿಜವಾದ ರೂಪವನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ ಎಂನ ನಂಬಿಕೆಯಿದೆ.

claims.statement: In the stories an ordinary male cobra becomes an ichchhadhari nag, and an ordinary female cobra becomes an ichchhadhari nagin after 100 years of penance.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita, kobra jantan biasa menjadi ichchhadhari nag, dan kobra betina biasa menjadi ichchhadhari nagin setelah 100 tahun bertapa.
claims.quote: ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಗಂಡು ನಾಗರಹಾವು ಇಚ್ಚಾಧಾರಿ ನಾಗ (ಗಂಡು ಆಕಾರವನ್ನು ಬದಲಾಯಿಸುವ ನಾಗರಹಾವು) ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಹೆಣ್ಣು ನಾಗರಹಾವು ೧೦೦ ವರ್ಷಗಳ ತಪಸ್ಸಿನ ನಂತರ ಇಚ್ಚಾಧಾರಿ ನಾಗಿನ್

claims.statement: In addition they gain the ability to take the form of any living creature.
claims.statement_id: Selain itu, mereka memperoleh kemampuan untuk mengambil bentuk makhluk hidup apa pun.
claims.quote: ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಇವು ಯಾವುದೇ ಜೀವಿಯ ಆಕಾರವನ್ನು ಹೊಂದುವ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯವನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.

claims.statement: They can live for more than a hundred years.

claims.statement: Legends say that people who try to steal the nagamani die of snakebite.
claims.statement_id: Legenda menyebut bahwa orang yang mencoba mencuri nagamani itu mati karena gigitan ular.
claims.quote: ಈ ನಾಗಮಣಿಯನ್ನು ಕದಿಯಲು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿದಾಗ ಆ ಜನರು ಹಾವು ಕಡಿತದಿಂದ ಸಾಯುತ್ತಾರೆ ಎಂದು ದಂತಕಥೆಗಳು ಹೇಳುತ್ತವೆ.

claims.statement: There is a belief that when a nag or nagin is killed, the killer's image is imprinted in its eyes; legends say its mate or family recognises the killer from this image and takes revenge.
claims.statement_id: Ada kepercayaan bahwa saat seekor nag atau nagin dibunuh, gambar si pembunuh tercetak di matanya; legenda menyebut pasangan atau keluarganya mengenali pembunuh dari gambar itu dan membalas dendam.
claims.quote: ಒಬ್ಬ ನಾಗ ಅಥವಾ ನಾಗಿಣಿಯನ್ನು ಕೊಲ್ಲುವಾಗ ಆ ಕೊಲೆಗಾರನ ಚಿತ್ರಣವು ಅವರ ಕಣ್ಣುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮುದ್ರಿಸಲ್ಪಡುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂಬ ನಂಬಿಕೆಯಿದೆ. ಆ ನಾಗ/ನಾಗಿಣಿಯ ಸಂಗಾತಿ ಅಥವಾ ಕುಟುಂಬವು ಈ ಚಿತ್ರದಿಂದ ಕೊಲೆಗಾರರನ್ನು ಗುರುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸೇಡು ತೀರಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂದು ದಂತಕತೆಗಳು ಹೇಳುತ್ತವೆ.

claims.statement: The enemies of the ichchhadhari nag/nagin are the mongoose, the eagle and the peacock.
claims.statement_id: Musuh ichchhadhari nag/nagin adalah luwak, elang, dan merak.

claims.statement_id: Dunia para nag dan nagin disebut Naglok, yang diperintah oleh Nagraj (raja) atau Nagrani (ratu).
claims.quote: ನಾಗಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ನಾಗಿನಗಳ ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ನಾಗ್ಲೋಕ್ ಎಂದು ಕರೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ನಾಗ್ಲೋಕ್ ಅನ್ನು ನಾಗರಾಜ್ (ರಾಜ) ಅಥವಾ ನಾಗ್ರಾಣಿ (ರಾಣಿ) ಆಳುತ್ತಾರೆ.

claims.quote: The nāga were thought to be powerful, having both good and evil qualities. These beings could shape-shift into human form so that they could walk through human cities undetected. They were thought to be able to grant immortality to those they favored.

claims.statement: According to this encyclopedia article, if angered nāgas might use venom to kill the offender, or destroy enemies by squeezing them as a boa constrictor might.

claims.quote: If angered, nāgas might use venom to kill the offender. Another way nāgas might destroy their enemies is by squeezing them, as a boa constrictor might.

claims.statement: Kallana names dwarf elephants reported by Kaani communities in South Indian forests.
claims.statement_id: Kallana adalah sebutan bagi gajah kerdil yang diklaim masyarakat Kaani berada di hutan India selatan.
claims.quote: Kallana is a suspected species of dwarf elephant allegedly found in South India. Kaani tribals dwelling in the rainforests of the Western Ghats (Kerala, India) claim that there are two distinct varieties of elephants in the Peppara forest range, one the common Indian elephants (Elephas maximus indicus), and the other a dwarf variety which they call kallana.

claims.statement: The name combines kallu, stones, and aana, elephant.
claims.statement_id: Nama ini menggabungkan kallu, batu, dan aana, gajah.
claims.quote: The name kallana comes from the words "kallu", which means stones or boulders, and "aana", which means elephant.

claims.statement: The existence of a distinct dwarf elephant variety in India has not been scientifically established.
claims.statement_id: Keberadaan jenis gajah kerdil tersendiri di India belum dipastikan secara ilmiah.
claims.quote: The existence of a pygmy variety of elephant in India is yet to be scientifically ascertained.

claims.statement: Some experts regard solitary sightings as potentially indicating a genetic anomaly rather than a separate species.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian ahli menilai penampakan hewan tunggal dapat menunjukkan kelainan genetik, bukan spesies terpisah.
claims.quote: Some of the criticisms from experts is that all the sightings have been of solitary animals. This could be a sign of genetic aberration rather than a separate species.

claims.statement: The tribals gave the creatures this name because they see the smaller elephant more often at higher altitudes where the terrain is rocky.

claims.quote: The tribals gave the creatures this name because they see the smaller elephant more often in the higher altitudes where the terrain is rocky.

claims.quote: On 17 March 2010, the same Mallan Kani guided the photographer Benny Ajantha to a kallana and he took pictures. This was reported in the Malayalam daily Malayala Manorama with a picture, but one needs to be captured and tested to see whether it is a separate species.

claims.quote: In 2013, a dwarf individual belonging to Elephas maximus was observed in Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka and scientifically documented.

claims.quote: one of the protagonists was a mature male of just over five feet (1.5 m) in height. It had a normal sized upper body ... but had very short, stubby legs.

claims.statement: Kao is a divine bull in Meitei mythology captured by Khuman Khamba.
claims.statement_id: Kao adalah banteng ilahi dalam mitologi Meitei yang ditangkap Khuman Khamba.
claims.quote: Kao (Meitei pronunciation: /káo/) is a legendary divine bull captured by Khuman Khamba in Meitei mythology and folklore of ancient Moirang realm.

claims.statement: The tale of its capture forms part of the Khamba Thoibi epic.
claims.statement_id: Kisah penangkapannya merupakan bagian dari epos Khamba Thoibi.
claims.quote: It appears in the legend of Kao Phaba (Old Manipuri: Kau Phaapa), also known as Khambana Kao Phaba (Old Manipuri: Khampana Kao Phaapa) of the Khamba Thoibi epic.

claims.statement: Kongyamba tricked his servant Khamba into catching the bull by pretending before the king that he was possessed by a divine spirit and claiming the god Thangjing spoke through him; he demanded the flesh of the bull terrorizing the people of Khuman, saying he was 'sated with offerings of flesh and fish'.
claims.statement_id: Kongyamba menipu pelayannya, Khamba, agar menangkap banteng itu dengan berpura-pura di hadapan raja bahwa ia dirasuki roh ilahi dan mengaku dewa Thangjing berbicara melaluinya; ia menuntut daging banteng yang meneror rakyat Khuman karena 'bosan dengan persembahan daging dan ikan'.
claims.quote: Kongyamba then tricked his servant Khamba into catching the bull, by pretending, before the king, that he was possessed by a divine spirit, and claimed that the god Thangjing spoke through him. Saying he was "sated with offerings of flesh and fish", he demanded to be given the flesh of the bull that was terrorizing the people of Khuman.

claims.statement: Khamnu tells Khamba that the bull once belonged to their father.
claims.statement_id: Khamnu memberi tahu Khamba bahwa banteng itu pernah milik ayah mereka.
claims.quote: Khamnu revealed a secret to Khamba. She said that the bull had once belonged to their father.  She told him that if Khamba told the bull their father's name, it would be tame and gentle:

claims.statement: After Khamba follows his sister's instructions, the bull becomes tame and is brought back.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Khamba menjalankan petunjuk kakaknya, banteng menjadi jinak dan dibawa kembali.
claims.quote: Khamba did everything as his sister had told him to do. Immediately, the wild bull became tame and gentle. Khamba brought the bull back.

claims.statement: Kongyamba, a rich nobleman of the Angom clan, met women from the Khuman kingdom in Moirang, who told him that a dangerous bull had killed many people near the water so they could not fish.
claims.statement_id: Kongyamba, bangsawan kaya dari klan Angom, bertemu sekelompok perempuan dari kerajaan Khuman di Moirang; mereka mengatakan seekor banteng berbahaya telah membunuh banyak orang di dekat air sehingga mereka tidak dapat memancing.
claims.quote: Kongyamba, a rich nobleman of the Angom clan, met a group of women from the Khuman kingdom in a place called Moirang, and asked them why they were fishing there. They told him that a dangerous bull had killed many people near the water, so they could not fish.

claims.statement: Khamba stood on firm ground and caught the bull, and the strong bull carried him away into the thick woods.
claims.statement_id: Khamba berdiri di tanah yang kokoh lalu menangkap banteng itu, dan banteng yang kuat itu membawanya pergi ke dalam hutan lebat.
claims.quote: Khamba answered that he was waiting for a good position. Then, he stood on firm ground and caught the bull. The strong bull carried him away into the thick woods.

claims.statement: On the way back Kongyamba came to Khamba before anyone saw them, pretended to help hold the bull and held the rope, then claimed that he had captured the bull.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perjalanan pulang, Kongyamba mendatangi Khamba sebelum ada yang melihat, berpura-pura membantu memegang banteng dan memegang tali, lalu mengaku dialah yang menangkap banteng itu.
claims.quote: On the way back, Kongyamba came to him before anyone saw them. Kongyamba pretended to help Khamba to hold the bull. Kongyamba held the rope. When everyone saw, Kongyamba claimed that he had captured the bull.

claims.statement: Kongyamba was afraid of the bull and climbed up to the heights to save himself, while Khamba faced the bull bravely and captured it once again.
claims.statement_id: Kongyamba takut pada banteng dan memanjat tempat tinggi untuk menyelamatkan diri, sedangkan Khamba menghadapi banteng dengan berani dan menangkapnya sekali lagi.
claims.quote: But Kongyamba was afraid of the bull. He climbed up on the heights to save himself. Khamba faced the bull bravely. He once again captured the bull.

claims.statement: The embassy proposed organizing the great sport of capturing the wild bull; the Khuman king agreed, and a grand colosseum was built for the event.
claims.statement_id: Utusan mengusulkan penyelenggaraan olahraga besar menangkap banteng liar; raja Khuman setuju, dan sebuah koloseum megah dibangun untuk acara itu.
claims.quote: The embassy proposed to organize the great sport of capturing the wild bull. The Khuman king agreed. A grand colosseum was built for the event.

claims.statement: In 2001 the painting Khambana Kao Phaba was kept in the permanent collection of the Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS) Museum in Bhopal, India.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2001, lukisan Khambana Kao Phaba disimpan dalam koleksi tetap Museum Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS) di Bhopal, India.
claims.quote: In 2001, Khambana Kao Phaba (painting) was kept in the permanent collection of the Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS) Museum, Bhopal, India.

claims.statement: In 2011 the theatre show 'Kao, the sacred bull' was produced by the Laihui Ensemble, based on the story of the bull Kao.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2011, pertunjukan teater 'Kao, the sacred bull' diproduksi oleh Laihui Ensemble berdasarkan kisah banteng Kao.
claims.quote: In 2011, "Kao, the sacred bull" was produced by the Laihui Ensemble. This theatrical show was based on the story of the bull Kao.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, the Khumal women say that a great bull lurks among the reeds bordering the waters of Waithou and has already killed a man, so they dare not fish there.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, para perempuan Khumal berkata bahwa seekor banteng besar mengintai di antara alang-alang di tepi perairan Waithou dan sudah membunuh seorang laki-laki, sehingga mereka tidak berani memancing di sana.
claims.quote: There is a great bull that lurks among the reeds that border the waters of Waithou, and already he has killed a man. So we dare not fish there.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, Khamnu, ill at ease for Khamba, says that this great bull was once the Lord of Khamba's father's herd.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamnu, yang gelisah memikirkan Khamba, berkata bahwa banteng besar itu dahulu adalah pemimpin kawanan ternak ayah Khamba.
claims.quote: Then Khamnu, who had treasured many things in her heart, was ill at ease for Khamba, and said, “ This great bull was once the Lord of thy father’s herd.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, Khamba stood on firm ground and caught the bull by the horns, they swayed together striving for mastery, and then Khamba rested on the bull's neck as it carried him into the jungle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba berdiri di tanah kokoh dan menangkap banteng pada tanduknya; mereka saling mendorong memperebutkan kekuasaan, lalu Khamba bertumpu di leher banteng yang membawanya ke dalam hutan.
claims.quote: Then he stood on firm ground and caught the bull by the horns, and they swayed together as they strove for the mastery. Then Khamba rested on the neck of the bull, who carried him into the jungle.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, Khamba softly spoke his father's name into the bull's ear and showed it the silken rope; the bull remembered the name of its Master, knew the rope and tied it round its own neck.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba membisikkan nama ayahnya ke telinga banteng dan menunjukkan tali suteranya; banteng teringat nama majikannya, mengenali tali itu, dan mengikatkannya sendiri di lehernya.
claims.quote: And Khamba spake his Father’s name softly into the ear of the bull, and showed him the silken rope. Then the bull remembered the name of his Master and knew the rope, and himself tied it round his own neck.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, on the next day Khamba killed the bull in honour of the God Thangjing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, keesokan harinya Khamba membunuh banteng itu untuk menghormati dewa Thangjing.
claims.quote: but the Moirang King would not, and on the morrow Khamba killed the bull in honour of the God Thangjing.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, Khamba fought the bull bravely; he suddenly caught it by the tail and then let go so that it fell on its knees.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba melawan banteng dengan berani; ia tiba-tiba memegang ekornya lalu melepaskannya sehingga banteng jatuh berlutut.
claims.quote: Then Khamba fought the bull bravely ; he caught it by the tail suddenly, and then on a sudden let it go so that it fell on its knees.

claims.statement: Pinglak is a lion character in the Panchatantra fables.
claims.statement_id: Pinglak adalah tokoh singa dalam kumpulan fabel Panchatantra.
claims.quote: Pinglak is a character in Panchatantra. It is a lion which is metaphorically called as Pinglak. It is hypothesis and the story is used to compare the real moral and relevant at present also. Panchatantra, a collection of stories which depict animals in human situations (see anthropomorphism, Talking animals in fiction).

claims.statement: His tale belongs to the Mitrabheda section about a lion and bull's broken friendship.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya berada dalam bagian Mitrabheda tentang rusaknya persahabatan singa dan banteng.
claims.quote: The first chapter is termed "Mitrabheda", which means betrayal of friends. This story is about a lion and a bull who became friends. Somehow, a dispute occurred between them and they both fought. Finally, one of them died.

claims.statement: Sanjeewak is a bull abandoned by his master in a forest when ill.
claims.statement_id: Sanjeewak adalah banteng yang ditinggalkan majikannya di hutan ketika sakit.
claims.quote: Sanjeewak was a bull who, because of his incapabilities and illness was discarded by his master and was left alone in a jungle, where he sat on the bank of Yamuna river and grew stronger.

claims.statement: His two advisers are the jackals Karkat and Damnak.
claims.statement_id: Dua penasihatnya adalah jakal Karkat dan Damnak.
claims.quote: The lion had two cunning jackal ministers named Karkat and Damnak.

claims.statement: Its original Indian version is Mitra-bheda, The Separation of Friends; in the first story a friendship arises between the lion Piṅgalaka, the king of the forest, and the bull Sañjīvaka; Karataka ('Horribly Howling') and Damanaka ('Victor') are two jackals who are retainers to the lion king.
claims.statement_id: Versi India aslinya adalah Mitra-bheda, 'Perpisahan Para Sahabat'. Dalam kisah pertama, persahabatan tumbuh antara singa Piṅgalaka, raja hutan, dan banteng Sañjīvaka; Karataka ('Si Penguik Mengerikan') dan Damanaka ('Sang Pemenang') adalah dua jakal pengikut raja singa itu.
claims.quote: Its original Indian version is Mitra-bheda, The Separation of Friends. In the first story, a friendship arises between the lion Piṅgalaka, the king of the forest, and Sañjīvaka, a bull. Karataka ('Horribly Howling') and Damanaka ('Victor') are two jackals that are retainers to the lion king.

claims.statement: Against Karataka's advice, Damanaka breaks up the friendship between the lion and the bull out of jealousy.
claims.statement_id: Melawan nasihat Karataka, Damanaka merusak persahabatan antara singa dan banteng karena iri.
claims.quote: Against Karataka's advice, Damanaka breaks up the friendship between the lion and the bull out of jealousy.

claims.statement: The lion indulged so deeply in the friendship that he left his entire kingship; when all the animals of the jungle felt insecure because of this, the jackals again managed to create differences between Pinglak and Sanjeewak.
claims.statement_id: Sang singa begitu tenggelam dalam persahabatan itu hingga meninggalkan seluruh kekuasaannya; ketika semua hewan hutan merasa tidak aman karenanya, para jakal kembali berhasil menimbulkan perselisihan antara Pinglak dan Sanjeewak.
claims.quote: The lion indulged so deeply in the friendship that he left his entire kingship. When all the animals in the jungle felt insecure due to this, then the jackals again managed to create differences between Pinglak and Sanjeewak.

claims.statement: In this text, in a neighbouring wood there lived a lion named Pingalaka who had subdued the forest by his might; that king of beasts had two jackals for ministers, named Damanaka and Karataka.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, di hutan yang bertetangga hidup seekor singa bernama Pingalaka yang menundukkan hutan dengan kekuatannya; raja binatang itu memiliki dua jakal sebagai menteri, bernama Damanaka dan Karataka.
claims.quote: Now at that time there lived in a neighbouring wood a lion named Pingalaka, who had subdued the forest by his might; and that king of beasts had two jackals for ministers; the name of the one was Damanaka, and the name of the other was Karataka.

claims.statement: In this text the lion, going to drink at the bank of the Yamuná, hears the roar of the bull Sanjívaka, quickly returns to the forest without drinking and stays in a state of fear, hiding his feelings from his followers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, singa itu mendengar raungan banteng Sanjívaka di tepi Yamuná saat hendak minum, lalu cepat kembali ke hutan tanpa minum dan tetap ketakutan sambil menyembunyikan perasaannya dari para pengikutnya.
claims.quote: That lion, going one day to the bank of the Yamuná to drink water, heard close to him the roar of that bull Sanjívaka. ... There upon the lion quickly returned to the forest without drinking water, and continued in a state of fear, hiding his feelings from his followers.

claims.statement: In this text the bull consented and gradually gained such an influence over the lion that the lion turned his back on his other dependents and was entirely governed by the bull.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, banteng menyetujui, dan lambat laun memperoleh pengaruh sedemikian besar atas singa sehingga singa membelakangi pengikut lainnya dan sepenuhnya dikuasai banteng.
claims.quote: And the bull consented, and gradually gained such an influence over the lion, that he turned his back on his other dependents, and was entirely governed by the bull.

claims.statement: In this text an annoyed Damanaka tells Karataka in secret that their master has been taken possession of by Sanjívaka and does not trouble his head about them, and that he will take steps to have the bull killed and to reclaim their master from his unbecoming infatuation.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, Damanaka yang kesal berkata diam-diam kepada Karataka bahwa tuan mereka telah dikuasai Sanjívaka dan tidak peduli pada mereka, dan ia akan mengambil langkah agar banteng itu dibunuh dan tuan mereka direbut kembali dari kegilaannya.
claims.quote: Then Damanaka, being annoyed, said to Karataka in secret: " See ! our master has been taken possession of by Sanjívaka, and does not trouble his head about us. ... So I will now take steps to have him killed, and to reclaim our master from his unbecoming infatuation.

claims.statement: In this text the lion sprang on the bull and struck him with his claws, the bull replied with his horns, and their fight went on.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, singa menerkam banteng dan mencakarnya, banteng membalas dengan tanduknya, dan pertarungan mereka berlanjut.
claims.quote: Then the lion sprang on the bull and struck him with his claws, the bull replied with his horns, and so their fight went on.

claims.statement: In this text the lion killed the bull Sanjívaka; once he was slain, Damanaka recovered his position of minister without a rival and remained for a long time beside the king of beasts in perfect happiness.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, singa membunuh banteng Sanjívaka; setelah banteng itu tewas, Damanaka kembali menjadi menteri tanpa saingan dan lama mendampingi raja binatang dengan sangat bahagia.
claims.quote: lion killed the bull Sanjívaka. When he was slain, Damanaka recovered his position of minister without a rival, and remained for a long time about the person of the king of beasts in perfect happiness.

claims.statement: Samaton is a winged divine horse of Meitei mythology.
claims.statement_id: Samaton adalah kuda ilahi bersayap dalam mitologi Meitei.
claims.quote: Samaton (/saa-ma-ton/) or Samadon (/saa-ma-don/) is a mythical winged divine horse in Meitei mythology. He is one of the most recognised creatures in Meitei folklore. Legend says that Samaton is the ancestor of the present day Manipuri pony (Meitei horse). The Leithak Leikharol describes Samaton as a primordial horse associated with Meitei cosmology.

claims.statement: Legend identifies him as the ancestor of the Manipuri pony.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ia adalah leluhur kuda poni Manipur.
claims.quote: Samaton (/saa-ma-ton/) or Samadon (/saa-ma-don/) is a mythical winged divine horse in Meitei mythology. He is one of the most recognised creatures in Meitei folklore. Legend says that Samaton is the ancestor of the present day Manipuri pony (Meitei horse). The Leithak Leikharol describes Samaton as a primordial horse associated with Meitei cosmology.

claims.statement: The Leithak Leikharol describes him as a primordial horse created by Sanamahi to attack Pakhangba.
claims.statement_id: Leithak Leikharol menggambarkannya sebagai kuda primordial yang dibuat Sanamahi untuk menyerang Pakhangba.
claims.quote: The Leithak Leikharol describes Samaton as a primordial horse associated with Meitei cosmology. It is created by Sanamahi to attack on Pakhangba.

claims.statement: He later becomes the mount of the god Marjing.
claims.statement_id: Ia kemudian menjadi tunggangan dewa Marjing.
claims.quote: Later, it became the mounting creature of God Marjing.

claims.statement: Samaton is praised in the Ougri ritual song sung during Lai Haraoba.
claims.statement_id: Samaton dipuji dalam lagu ritual Ougri yang dinyanyikan pada Lai Haraoba.
claims.quote: Samaton is praised in the ritual song of Ougri sung during the Lai Haraoba festival. Samaton is considered very important to Meitei culture because it is created from the body of God Sanamahi. During the deification of Meitei kings, Samaton became associated with kings as it was a divine being. So, Samaton became the insignia of royalty.

claims.statement: Ranjit Singh records Hada Samaton Ayangba as a theme song for a Manipur polo tournament.
claims.statement_id: Ranjit Singh mencatat lagu Hada Samaton Ayangba sebagai lagu tema turnamen polo Manipur.
claims.quote: a musical sensation was created in the Manipuri music world by Mangka with her solo song "Hada Samaton Ayangba" The song specially composed as Theme Song of the 8th Manipur Polo International 2014

claims.statement: Sanbo Kojin is a god of fire, the hearth and the kitchen in Japanese tradition.
claims.statement_id: Sanbo Kojin adalah dewa api, perapian, dan dapur dalam tradisi Jepang.
claims.quote: Kōjin, also known as Sambō-Kōjin or Sanbō-Kōjin (三宝荒神), is the Japanese kami (god) of fire, the hearth and the kitchen.  He is sometimes called Kamado-gami (竃神), literally the god of the stove. He represents violent forces that are turned toward the betterment of humankind.

claims.statement: Kojin embodies fire controlled and used for a good purpose.
claims.statement_id: Kojin mewakili api yang dikendalikan dan digunakan untuk tujuan baik.
claims.quote: However, Kōjin embodies fire controlled and turned toward a good purpose.

claims.statement: He is believed to destroy impurity and watch over the household.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya menghancurkan ketidakmurnian dan mengawasi rumah tangga.
claims.quote: He is said to destroy all impurity. He is also responsible for watching over the household and reporting any misdeeds to the kami of the village or city.

claims.statement: He is sometimes identified with Fudo Myo-o.
claims.statement_id: Ia kadang diidentifikasi dengan Fudo Myo-o.
claims.quote: Kōjin is sometimes identified as an incarnation of Fudō Myō-Ō, who is likewise depicted as surrounded by flames and tasked with dealing with misdeeds.

claims.statement: His representation is traditionally placed near the hearth.
claims.statement_id: Representasinya secara tradisional ditempatkan di dekat perapian.
claims.quote: Traditionally, a representation of Kōjin is placed near the hearth.  This representation might be a simple fuda (memorial tablet) in many homes, or it might be as elaborate as a statue, as is common in Buddhist temples.  In his statues, Kōjin is depicted with flaming hair, fangs, and a contorted face, and he often wields a bow and arrows.  He has two pairs of hands.

claims.statement: JAANUS describes Kojin as a god protecting against disaster and bringing good fortune.
claims.statement_id: JAANUS menyebut Kojin sebagai dewa yang melindungi dari bencana dan membawa keberuntungan.
claims.quote: A god that protects against disaster and brings good fortune.

claims.statement: Banjhakri and Banjhakrini are shamanic deities in Kirati tradition in Nepal and the Indian areas named by the source.
claims.statement_id: Banjhakri dan Banjhakrini adalah sosok ilahi perdukunan dalam tradisi Kirati di Nepal dan kawasan India yang disebut sumber.
claims.quote: Banjhākri and Banjhākrini are shamanic deities in the tradition of the Kirati people of Nepal and Sikkim, Darjeeling, and Kalimpong in India. They are a couple, and possibly different aspects of the same being. They are supernatural shamans of the forest. In the Nepali language, ban means "wilderness", jhākri means "shaman", and jhākrini means "shamaness".

claims.statement: They are a couple understood as supernatural shamans of the forest.
claims.statement_id: Mereka adalah pasangan dan dipahami sebagai dukun supranatural hutan.
claims.quote: They are a couple, and possibly different aspects of the same being. They are supernatural shamans of the forest.

claims.statement: Banjhakri is portrayed as short and hairy with large ears and backward-pointing feet.
claims.statement_id: Banjhakri digambarkan bertubuh pendek, berbulu, bertelinga besar, dan berkaki terbalik.
claims.quote: Banjhākri is a short, wild, simian trickster who is a descendant of the Sun. His ears are large and his feet point backward. Long, matted hair covers his entire body, except for his face and palms, and he plays a golden dhyāngro. The dhyangro is the frame drum played by Nepali jhākri.

claims.statement: He takes children with shamanic potential to his cave for training.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa anak berpotensi menjadi dukun ke guanya untuk pelatihan.
claims.quote: Banjhākri finds human children who have the potential to be great shamans, and takes them back to his cave for training.

claims.statement: Children who pass Banjhakrini's initiation return with shamanic training.
claims.statement_id: Anak yang lolos inisiasi Banjhakrini kembali dengan kemampuan perdukunan.
claims.quote: He trains the children who pass Banjhākrini's initiation. When the children return home with their shamanic training, they can become more powerful than the shamans trained by people.

claims.statement: According to this article, nearly all caste-based traditions of shamanism in the region consider banjhakri the original guru of all shamans and the source of all shamanic knowledge.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, hampir semua tradisi perdukunan berbasis kasta di kawasan itu menganggap banjhakri sebagai guru asal semua dukun dan sumber seluruh pengetahuan perdukunan.
claims.quote: Nearly all caste-based traditions of shamanism in the region consider banjhakri as the original guru of all shamans and the source of all shamanic knowledge.

claims.statement: Banjhakri is associated with deep mountainous forests and is often thought to reside in caves, caverns, big cliffs, sources of springs, and behind waterfalls.
claims.statement_id: Banjhakri dikaitkan dengan hutan pegunungan yang dalam dan sering dipercaya tinggal di gua, ceruk besar, tebing besar, mata air, dan di balik air terjun.
claims.quote: Associated with deep mountainous forests, banjhakri is often thought to reside in caves, caverns, big cliffs, sources of springs, and behind the waterfalls.

claims.statement: Banjhakri is universally described as a short ape-like man with a conical golden head, red face, long ears, long tangled hair all over his body, and a long white beard.
claims.statement_id: Banjhakri digambarkan secara universal sebagai lelaki pendek mirip kera, berkepala kerucut keemasan, berwajah merah, bertelinga panjang, berambut panjang kusut di sekujur tubuh, dan berjanggut putih panjang.
claims.quote: He is universally described as a short ape-like man, with a conical golden head, red face, long ears, long tangled hair all over his body and a long white beard

claims.statement: To impart his recondite shamanic knowledge, a banjhakri kidnaps 'unblemished' young people and trains them for an uncertain period ranging from a couple of days to months.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menurunkan pengetahuan perdukunannya yang rahasia, banjhakri menculik anak muda yang 'tanpa cela' dan melatih mereka selama waktu yang tidak pasti, dari beberapa hari hingga berbulan-bulan.
claims.quote: To impart his recondite shamanic knowledge, a banjhakri kidnaps “unblemished” young people and trains them for an uncertain period of time, ranging from a couple of days to months.

claims.statement: Almost all accounts describe banjhakri as a kind and intelligent teacher.
claims.statement_id: Hampir semua kisah menggambarkan banjhakri sebagai guru yang baik hati dan cerdas.
claims.quote: Nevertheless, almost all accounts describe banjhakri as a kind and intelligent teacher.

claims.statement: In sharp contrast with banjhakri, his consort banjhakrini is described as a big beastly creature with long saggy breasts, violent in nature and fond of devouring human flesh.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda tajam dari banjhakri, pasangannya, banjhakrini, digambarkan sebagai makhluk besar buas berpayudara panjang menggantung, bersifat kejam, dan gemar memakan daging manusia.
claims.quote: This is a sharp contrast with his consort, banjhakrini, who is described as a big beastly creature, with long saggy breasts, who is violent in nature and loves to devour human flesh

claims.statement: Banjhakri has to constantly dominate his wife through his power so that she would not eat his pupils.

claims.quote: In folklore, she is considered a conniving seducer of men, a robber of children and a wild misogynist trying to murder and disfigure unassuming women that she takes by surprise.

claims.quote: The Raantas is believed to possess some magic, with the ability to disguise herself as any human being, which gives her the power to deceive anyone.

claims.statement: In the Rigveda account Indra destroys Susna's fortress and sends rain at Kutsa's request.

claims.quote: He brake in pieces Susna's brood who still expected not the stroke, and won for us the heavenly streams.
