claims.quote: In Journey to the West, when Sun Wukong was arguing with the fake Sun Wukong, they went to Diyu to seek help. Ksitigarbha referred the monkeys to his steed Diting, given the latter's ability to differentiate all creatures in the world.

claims.statement: Diting was able to distinguish the true monkey, but knew the fake monkey would wreak havoc in his abode once exposed, so he asked Ksitigarbha to send the pair to Buddha instead.
claims.statement_id: Diting dapat membedakan kera yang asli, tetapi ia tahu kera palsu akan mengamuk di tempat tinggalnya jika terbongkar, sehingga ia meminta Ksitigarbha mengirim keduanya kepada Buddha.
claims.quote: Diting was able to distinguish the true monkey, but he knew the fake monkey will wreak havoc in his abode once exposed, so he asked Ksitigarbha to send the duo to Buddha instead.

claims.statement: One interpretation holds that Diting's single horn could receive information across the universe and could also be used to attack and defend.
claims.statement_id: Satu tafsir menyebut tanduk tunggal Diting dapat menerima informasi di seluruh alam semesta dan juga dapat dipakai untuk menyerang dan bertahan.
claims.quote: Diting (Chinese: 谛听; pinyin: Dìtīng; Vietnamese: Đế Thính) ... One interpretation of its single horn was that it could receive information across the universe. It could also be used to attack and defend.

claims.statement: Its hound ears were likened to a universal radio, transmitting the ability to distinguish good from bad to all believers.
claims.statement_id: Telinganya yang mirip telinga anjing pemburu diibaratkan radio universal yang menyalurkan kemampuan membedakan baik dari buruk kepada semua penganut.
claims.quote: Diting (Chinese: 谛听; pinyin: Dìtīng; Vietnamese: Đế Thính) ... Its hound ears were like a universal radio, transmitting the ability to distinguish good from bad to all believers.

claims.statement: In some tales, before leaving Heaven to begin a new life as a monk, Kṣitigarbha found that his mother from a past life would be reborn as a dog.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian kisah, sebelum meninggalkan Surga untuk menjalani hidup baru sebagai biksu, Kṣitigarbha mendapati bahwa ibunya di kehidupan lampau akan terlahir kembali sebagai anjing.
claims.quote: In some tales, before Kṣitigarbha left Heaven to assume his new life as a monk, he found that his mother from his past life would be reborn as a dog.

claims.statement: The dog followed the dharma as well and often acted as Ksitigarbha's guard.
claims.statement_id: Anjing itu juga mengikuti dharma dan sering bertindak sebagai penjaga Ksitigarbha.
claims.quote: The dog followed the dharma as well and often acted as Ksitigarbha's guard.

claims.statement: In this Chinese text Diting (諦聽) is the name of a beast that crouches beneath the scripture table of the Bodhisattva Dizang; when it lies on the ground it can in an instant discern good and evil and judge the wise and the foolish among many kinds of beings and immortals across the four great continents.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks Tionghoa ini, Diting (諦聽) adalah nama seekor hewan yang bersujud di bawah meja kitab Bodhisattva Dizang; bila ia berbaring di tanah, dalam sekejap ia dapat menilai baik dan buruk serta mendengar-menilai yang bijak dan yang bodoh di antara berbagai makhluk dan para dewa abadi di empat benua besar.
claims.quote: 原來那諦聽是地藏菩薩經案下伏的一個獸名。他若伏在地下，一霎時，將四大部洲山川社稷，洞天福地之間，蠃蟲、鱗蟲、毛蟲、羽蟲、昆蟲、天仙、地仙、神仙、人仙、鬼仙，可以照鑒善惡，察聽賢愚。

claims.statement: In this text, at Dizang's command the beast lay prostrate in the courtyard and, after a moment, raised its head and said that the monster's name exists but cannot be spoken to its face and that it cannot help to capture it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, atas perintah Dizang hewan itu bersujud di halaman istana lalu sejenak kemudian mengangkat kepala dan berkata bahwa nama siluman itu ada, tetapi tidak boleh dikatakan di hadapannya dan ia tidak dapat membantu menangkapnya.
claims.quote: 那獸奉地藏鈞旨，就於森羅庭院之中，俯伏在地。須臾，擡起頭來，對地藏道：「怪名雖有，但不可當面說破，又不能助力擒他。」

claims.statement: In this text Diting explains that naming the demon to its face might make it erupt and disturb the palace and unsettle the underworld, and that it cannot help capture it because the demon's powers equal those of the Great Sage Sun (孫大聖) while the deities of the underworld have little power.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, Diting menjelaskan bahwa menyebut nama itu di hadapan siluman dapat membuatnya mengamuk dan mengusik istana serta membuat dunia bawah gelisah, dan bahwa ia tidak dapat membantu menangkapnya karena kesaktian siluman itu setara Sun Dasheng (Orang Suci Agung Sun) sedangkan dewa-dewa alam gelap tidak punya banyak kekuatan.
claims.quote: 諦聽道：「當面說出，恐妖精惡發，搔擾寶殿，致令陰府不安。」又問：「何為不能助力擒拿？」諦聽道：「妖精神通，與孫大聖無二。幽冥之神，能有多少法力？故此不能擒拿。」

claims.statement: In this text Diting says the Buddha's law is boundless; Dizang at once understands and tells the two monkeys that to tell them apart they must go to the Leiyin Temple, to Sakyamuni Tathagata.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, Diting berkata bahwa hukum Buddha tak bertepi; Dizang segera memahami dan berkata kepada kedua kera bahwa untuk membedakan mereka harus pergi ke Kuil Leiyin, ke tempat Sakyamuni Tathagata.
claims.quote: 諦聽言：「佛法無邊。」地藏早已省悟，即對行者道：「你兩個形容如一，神通無二，若要辨明，須到雷音寺釋迦如來那裡，方得明白。」

claims.statement: Diting appears in the Chinese manhua and animated series Fabulous Beasts (有兽焉) as chief executive officer of the Underworld and the Underworld's Goods and Shipping, brother to the hellhound Qinghuo and father to the skeleton cat Kulou.
claims.statement_id: Diting muncul dalam manhua dan serial animasi Tiongkok Fabulous Beasts (有兽焉) sebagai direktur utama Dunia Bawah dan Perusahaan Barang dan Pengiriman Dunia Bawah, saudara anjing neraka Qinghuo dan ayah kucing kerangka Kulou.
claims.quote: Diting appears in the Chinese manhua and animated series Fabulous Beasts (有兽焉), as the chief executive officer of the Underworld and the Underworld's Goods and Shipping, brother to the clay-borne hellhound Qinghuo, and father to the skeleton cat Kulou.

issues.message: Tidak muncul di kutipan mana pun: Buddhas. Tambahkan klaim yang kutipannya memuat hal ini, atau hapus dari teks.

claims.statement: Buddhism recognises a protective divine group called the Eight Great Yaksa Generals.
claims.statement_id: Delapan jenderal yaksa merupakan kelompok pelindung ilahi dalam Buddhisme.
claims.quote: The Eight Great Yakṣa Generals (Chinese: 八大夜叉大将; pinyin: Bādà Yèchā Dàjiàng), or simply the Eight Yakṣa Generals, are guardian deities in Buddhism. They are retainers of Vaiśravaṇa, guardian of the north and king of the yakṣas.

claims.statement: They serve Vaisravana, who rules the yakshas and safeguards the northern direction.
claims.statement_id: Mereka melayani Vaisravana, yang berkuasa atas para yaksa dan menjaga arah utara.
claims.quote: They are retainers of Vaiśravaṇa, guardian of the north and king of the yakṣas.

claims.statement: In East Asia they are also known as the Eight Great Heavenly Kings.
claims.statement_id: Di Asia Timur mereka juga dikenal sebagai Eight Great Heavenly Kings.
claims.quote: In East Asia, they are also variously known as the Eight Great Yakṣas (八大藥叉), the Eight Great Heavenly Kings (八大天王), and the Eight Brothers of Vaiśravaṇa (毘沙門八兄弟).

claims.statement: A conversion narrative transforms formerly malevolent spirits into benevolent guardians.
claims.statement_id: Narasi pertobatan mengubah roh yang dahulu jahat menjadi dewa penjaga yang baik.
claims.quote: Originally malevolent beings, their conversion led to their deification as benevolent guardian deities.

claims.statement: The generals rank at the top among yakshas serving Vaisravana.
claims.statement_id: Para jenderal itu ditempatkan pada tingkat tertinggi di antara yaksa yang melayani Vaisravana.
claims.quote: Among the many yakṣas under Vaiśravaṇa's rule, the Eight Great Yakṣa Generals are ranked at the top of the hierarchy. Always at Vaiśravaṇa's command, these deities command 36,000 yakṣas that serve their king and are said to protect those who venerate them. A similar list may be found among the Twenty-Eight Great Yakṣa Generals.

claims.statement: According to Buddhist mythology, Vaiśravaṇa is the chief of these beings and long ago dwelt together with them in the realm of darkness; when he converted to Buddhism, the many demonic spirits under his jurisdiction likewise became devotees of the Buddha.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitologi Buddha, Vaiśravaṇa adalah kepala makhluk-makhluk ini dan dahulu tinggal bersama mereka di alam kegelapan; ketika Vaiśravaṇa memeluk agama Buddha, banyak roh iblis di bawah kekuasaannya juga menjadi pengikut Sang Buddha.
claims.quote: According to Buddhist mythology, Vaiśravaṇa is the chief of these beings, and long ago dwelt together with them in the realm of darkness. When Vaiśravaṇa converted to Buddhism, the many demonic spirits under his jurisdiction likewise assumed the role of devotees to the Buddha.

claims.statement: Always at Vaiśravaṇa's command, these deities command 36,000 yakṣas who serve their king and are said to protect those who venerate them.
claims.statement_id: Selalu berada di bawah perintah Vaiśravaṇa, para dewa ini memimpin 36.000 yaksa yang melayani raja mereka dan dikatakan melindungi orang-orang yang menghormati mereka.
claims.quote: Always at Vaiśravaṇa's command, these deities command 36,000 yakṣas that serve their king and are said to protect those who venerate them.

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, yasha also act as attendants of Bishamonten (毘沙門天), who is said to have 'eight yasha generals' (yasha hachidaishō, 夜叉八大将) under his command.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, yasha juga bertindak sebagai pengiring Bishamonten (毘沙門天), yang dikatakan memiliki "delapan jenderal yasha" (yasha hachidaishō, 夜叉八大将) di bawah komandonya.
claims.quote: They also act as attendants of *Bishamonten 毘沙門天, who is said to have under his command “eight yasha generals” yasha hachidaishō 夜叉八大将.

claims.statement: According to this paper's abstract, a mandala of Vaiśravaṇa and the eight yakṣas is painted on the south wall of the winding corridor in Cave 5 of the East Thousand Buddha Caves at Anxi; the author found this subject at no other cave including Mogao, its textual basis is not in Chinese-translated scriptures, and it is a new subject of the Xixia period influenced by Tibetan tantric Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: Menurut abstrak makalah ini, mandala Vaiśravaṇa dan delapan yaksa dilukis di dinding selatan lorong keliling Gua 5 di Gua Seribu Buddha Timur, Anxi; temanya tidak ditemukan di Mogao atau gua lain, tidak berdasar kitab terjemahan Tionghoa, dan merupakan tema baru zaman Xixia yang dipengaruhi Buddhisme tantra Tibet.
claims.quote: 安西東千佛洞第5窟繞道南向壁面所畫毗沙門天王及八大夜叉曼荼羅,據筆者的初步調查,該題材不見於莫高窟及其它石窟,其經典依據亦不見於漢譯經典,為西夏時代受藏傳密教影響的一個新的題材。

claims.statement: Enma is a Japanese god regarded as the king of hell.
claims.statement_id: Enma adalah dewa Jepang yang dipandang sebagai raja neraka.
claims.quote: est le dieu japonais et le roi d'enfer dans la mythologie japonaise

claims.statement: This source associates his statue near Kamakura with Unkei.
claims.statement_id: Sumber ini mengaitkan patungnya di dekat Kamakura dengan Unkei.
claims.quote: Sa statue siège dans un temple situé à proximité de Kamakura au Japon. Elle aurait été sculptée par le célèbre artiste Unkei.

claims.statement: According to the legend, when Unkei died he was summoned before the tribunal of Enma-o, who told him that he had made many portraits of him but none resembled him, and told him to go back and make a good portrait.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ketika Unkei meninggal ia dipanggil menghadap pengadilan Enma-o, yang berkata bahwa ia telah membuat banyak potret dirinya tetapi tak satu pun mirip, lalu menyuruhnya kembali ke dunia dan membuat potret yang bagus.
claims.quote: Lorsqu'Unkei mourut, il fut cité à comparaître devant le tribunal d'Enma-o qui lui dit : « Vous avez réalisé de nombreux portraits de ma personne tout au long de votre vie sur la Terre ; mais aucun ne me ressemble. Maintenant que vous m'avez vu de vos propres yeux, retournez-y et faites de moi un bon portrait. »

claims.statement: The tale says Unkei returned to Earth and made the temple statue.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu menyatakan Unkei kembali ke bumi dan menghasilkan patung kuil.
claims.quote: La légende dit que Unkei revint sur Terre et réalisa la fameuse statue qui orne le temple près de Kamakura.

claims.statement: Besides Enma, he is also called Enma-ō (閻魔王) or Enma-daiō (閻魔大王).
claims.statement_id: Selain Enma, ia juga disebut Enma-ō (閻魔王) atau Enma-daiō (閻魔大王).
claims.quote: Enma-ō (閻魔王) ou Enma-daiō (閻魔大王) est le dieu japonais et le roi d'enfer dans la mythologie japonaise

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, the Ten Kings are the ten kings of hell who preside at the gates of the underworld, assigning souls to heaven or hell.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, Sepuluh Raja adalah sepuluh raja neraka yang bertugas di gerbang dunia bawah, menetapkan jiwa ke surga atau neraka.
claims.quote: Ten Kings. The ten kings of hell who preside at the gates of the underworld, assigning souls to heaven or hell.

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, the Buddhist idea of hell derived from the Daoist underworld headed by Taishanfujun and his ten attendants; by the Tang dynasty this folk deity was associated with the Indian god Yama (Jp: Enmaō), the Lord of Death, incorporated into popular Chinese Buddhism, and then imported into Japan during the Heian period.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, gagasan neraka Buddhis berasal dari dunia bawah Tao yang dipimpin Taishanfujun dan sepuluh pengiringnya; pada zaman Tang dewa rakyat ini dikaitkan dengan dewa India Yama (Jp: Enmaō), Penguasa Kematian, dimasukkan ke Buddhisme Tiongkok populer, lalu diimpor ke Jepang pada zaman Heian.
claims.quote: The Buddhist idea of hell derived from the Daoist underworld headed by Taishanfujun (Jp: Taizanfukun 太山府君) and his ten attendants. By the Tang dynasty, this folk deity was associated with the Indian god Yama (Jp: *Enmaō 閻魔王), the Lord of Death, and incorporated into popular Chinese Buddhism, and then imported into Japan during the Heian period.

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, the Ten Kings usually sit in front of desks and wear the caps and robes of Chinese officials, but their faces, distorted by bulging eyes and grimacing mouths, reveal their terrifying function.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, Sepuluh Raja umumnya duduk di depan meja dan memakai topi serta jubah pejabat Tiongkok, tetapi wajah mereka yang cacat oleh mata melotot dan mulut meringis menunjukkan fungsi mereka yang menakutkan.
claims.quote: Typically the Ten Kings are rendered in painting on sets of ten hanging scrolls or in ten wooden sculptures. They usually sit in front of desks, and wear the caps and robes of Chinese officials. However, their faces, distorted by bulging eyes and grimacing mouths, reveal their terrifying function.

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, each king is associated with its true nature in the form of a Buddha (honjibutsu), and Enmaō is listed as the fifth king, paired with Jizō.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, tiap raja dikaitkan dengan wujud hakikinya sebagai Buddha (honjibutsu), dan Enmaō terdaftar sebagai raja kelima dengan Jizō di sisinya.
claims.quote: each king is also associated with its true nature in the form of a Buddha *honjibutsu 本地仏. ... 5 Enmaō (Ch: Yanlowang) / 57th day: Jizō.

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, with the rise of popular sects and the cult of Jizō, fear of hell became prominent in 13th-century Japanese Buddhism, and many temples built worship halls called enmadō (閻魔堂) with paintings or sculpture of the jūō inside.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, seiring bangkitnya sekte populer dan pemujaan Jizō, ketakutan akan neraka menonjol dalam Buddhisme Jepang abad ke-13, dan banyak kuil membangun aula pemujaan bernama enmadō (閻魔堂) berisi lukisan atau patung jūō.
claims.quote: With the rise of popular sects and the cult of Jizō, the fear of hell became a prominent feature in 13th-century Japanese Buddhism. Many temples built worship halls called enmadō 閻魔堂, with paintings or sculpture of the jūō placed inside.

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, the Ten Kings and Enmaō in particular were parodied by late Edo period artists such as Kawanabe Kyōsai (1831-89).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, Sepuluh Raja dan Enmaō secara khusus diparodikan oleh seniman akhir zaman Edo seperti Kawanabe Kyōsai (1831-89).
claims.quote: The Ten Kings and Enmaō, in particular, were parodied by late Edo period artists such as Kawanabe Kyōsai 河鍋暁斎 (1831-89).

claims.statement: Haosi Namoinu is a Meitei folktale figure who becomes an insect after her stepmother mistreats her.
claims.statement_id: Haosi Namoinu adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Meitei yang berubah menjadi serangga setelah disiksa ibu tiri.
claims.quote: Haosi Namoinu is a character in Meitei mythology and folklore of Kangleipak in India. After being mistreated by her stepmother, she transforms into a cicada (or cricket, depending on the version) and flies away from the human world.

claims.statement: Her insect form varies by version between cicada and cricket.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk serangganya berbeda menurut versi, berupa tonggeret atau jangkrik.
claims.quote: she transforms into a cicada (or cricket, depending on the version) and flies away from the human world.

claims.statement: She is the daughter of Pokmabi Laoshigam Chanu and Senbi Loikenba.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah putri Pokmabi Laoshigam Chanu dan Senbi Loikenba.
claims.quote: She was the only daughter of Lady Pokmabi Laoshigam Chanu and Lord Senbi Loikenba. Her father was a minister of Ancient Moirang, in charge of collecting tributes from the land of Kabo (present day Western Myanmar).

claims.statement: Her father remarries her mother's sister after her mother dies.
claims.statement_id: Ayahnya menikah kembali dengan saudari ibunya setelah sang ibu meninggal.
claims.quote: After Haosi Namoinu's mother's untimely death, her father remarried to Nganurol Laoshigam Chanu (Loisingam Chanu), her mother's sister.

claims.statement: Her stepmother forces her to husk rice, cook and serve food.
claims.statement_id: Ibu tirinya memaksa ia mengupas padi, memasak, dan menyajikan makanan.
claims.quote: She was forced to husk rice, cook food, and serve it.

claims.statement: Her story appears in the Khongjomnubi Nongarol.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya disebut dalam Khongjomnubi Nongarol.
claims.quote: The story of lady Haosi Namoinu is mentioned  in the Khongjomnubi Nongarol as one of its two content stories. The following is a passage from the text:

claims.statement: In this version, a man named Haoku Pakhang is left by his wife when his daughter is still very young, and he names his daughter Haoshi Namoinu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, seorang laki-laki bernama Haoku Pakhang ditinggal istrinya ketika putrinya masih sangat kecil, dan ia menamai putrinya Haoshi Namoinu.
claims.quote: Once upon a time there was a man named Haoku Pakhang. His wife left a daughter behind when his daughter was still very young. He named her daughter Haoshi Namoinu.

claims.statement: In this version the stepmother forces her stepdaughter to do all the work: chopping wood, collecting vegetables, dishing and cooking food, and gathering paddy and many vegetables from the field.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, ibu tiri memaksa anak tirinya mengerjakan semua pekerjaan: membelah kayu, mengumpulkan sayur, menyajikan dan memasak makanan, serta mengambil padi dan aneka sayuran dari ladang.
claims.quote: Chopping of woods, collecting vegetables, dishing, cooking, and on top of that she was sent to gather paddies from the field, and to gather many different vegetables, each and every work was forced to be done by her step-daughter.

claims.statement: In this version, instead of praising her hard work, the stepmother scolded her and beat her with kitchen utensils.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, bukannya memuji kerja kerasnya, ibu tirinya memarahi dan memukulnya dengan perkakas dapur.
claims.quote: Instead of praising for her hard work, her stepmother scolded her and beat her with kitchen utensils.

claims.statement: In this version, she says it is better to turn herself into a Harinongnang and hide in the trees; by saying this she was turned into a Harinongnang and flew towards the farthest hill.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, ia berkata lebih baik ia menjadi Harinongnang dan bersembunyi di pepohonan; setelah mengucapkannya ia berubah menjadi Harinongnang dan terbang ke bukit yang paling jauh.
claims.quote: She said that it is better to turn herself to Harinongnang and hide herself in the trees, in their sounds of 'neng neng'. By saying this, she was turned to Harinongnang and flew towards the farthest hill.

claims.statement: In this version, Haoshi Namoinu could bear her stepmother's hatred no more and was at last turned into a Harinongnang.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, Haoshi Namoinu tidak tahan lagi menghadapi kebencian ibu tirinya dan akhirnya berubah menjadi Harinongnang.
claims.quote: The poor Haoshi Namoinu cannot take any more hatred of her stepmother; she was at last turned into a Harinongnang.

claims.statement: Hingchabi is a creature of Meitei mythology, folklore and religion in Kangleipak.
claims.statement_id: Hingchabi adalah makhluk dalam mitologi, cerita rakyat, dan agama Meitei di Kangleipak.
claims.quote:
A Hingchabi (Meitei: ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯕꯤ, Old Manipuri: ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯄꯤ, romanized: hing-chaa-pee, lit. 'giantess') is a mythical creature in Meitei mythology, folklore and religion (Sanamahism) of Antique Kangleipak (Ancient Manipur). She has characters similar to those of the vampires as well as the witches.
The terms, "hing" means "raw" and "chaa" means "to eat" in Meitei language (Manipuri language).

claims.statement: The source compares her characteristics with vampires and witches.
claims.statement_id: Sumber membandingkan sifatnya dengan vampir dan penyihir.
claims.quote: She has characters similar to those of the vampires as well as the witches.

claims.statement: In Meitei, hing means raw and chaa means to eat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Meitei, hing berarti mentah dan chaa berarti makan.
claims.quote: The terms, "hing" means "raw" and "chaa" means "to eat" in Meitei language (Manipuri language).

claims.statement: In a footnote this ethnography glosses Hing-cha-bi as hing = living, cha = to eat, bi = honorific or respectful suffix, that is, 'that which eats living persons'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan kaki, Hodson menguraikan Hing-cha-bi sebagai hing = hidup, cha = makan, bi = akhiran hormat; yaitu 'yang memakan orang hidup'.
claims.quote: Hing-cha-bi (hing = living, cha = to eat, bi = honorific or respectful suffix), that which eats living persons.

claims.statement: In this ethnography, the vast crowd of 'hing-chabis' or vampires ('that which eats live men') and demons are beings the people believe in and fear, and fear is the basis of the ritual by which they try to propitiate them.
claims.statement_id: Dalam etnografi ini, kerumunan besar 'hing-chabi' atau vampir ('yang memakan orang hidup') dan iblis termasuk makhluk yang dipercaya dan ditakuti orang, dan ketakutan itu menjadi dasar ritual yang berusaha menenangkan mereka.
claims.quote: vast crowd of hing-cliabis or vampires (king = alive, clia = to eat, that which eats live men), lais liellois, or demons, in which the people believe and, fear being the basis of their ritual, which they try to propitiate.

claims.statement: According to this article the Meiteis have a firm belief in magical power, evil spirits, black magic and witchcraft; Hellois (witches), Hingchabis (vampires) and Saroi Ngaroi (evil spirits) are believed to occupy the outside world, so elders restrict movements on certain days and times to avoid unwanted happenings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, orang Meitei sangat percaya pada kekuatan gaib, roh jahat, ilmu hitam, dan sihir; Hellois (penyihir), Hingchabis (vampir), dan Saroi Ngaroi (roh jahat) dipercaya menempati dunia luar, sehingga para tetua membatasi pergerakan pada hari dan waktu tertentu untuk menghindari kejadian tak diinginkan.
claims.quote: The Meiteis have a firm belief in magical power, evil spirits, black magic, oracle, witchcraft and evil eyes. ... Hellois (witches), Hingchabis (vampires) and Saroi Ngaroi (evil spirit) are elements which are believed to occupy the outside world. Due to this reason, the elders restrict movements on certain days and time to avoid unwanted happenings.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the name is written ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯕꯤ in Meitei and ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯄꯤ in Old Manipuri, romanized hing-chaa-pee, literally 'giantess'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, nama itu ditulis ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯕꯤ dalam bahasa Meitei dan ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯄꯤ dalam Manipuri Lama, dilatinkan hing-chaa-pee, secara harfiah 'raksasi'.
claims.quote: (Meitei: ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯕꯤ, Old Manipuri: ꯍꯤꯡꯆꯥꯄꯤ, romanized: hing-chaa-pee, lit. 'giantess')

claims.statement: Hiyang Athouba is a Meitei folktale being arising from a corpse transformed into a monstrous creature.
claims.statement_id: Hiyang Athouba adalah sosok dari cerita rakyat Meitei yang berasal dari mayat berubah menjadi makhluk mengerikan.
claims.quote: It refers to a corpse that transforms into a demon-like, monstrous, or vampire-like being.

claims.statement: It belongs to the Lai Phattaba beings, evil spirits in Meitei belief.
claims.statement_id: Ia termasuk makhluk Lai Phattaba, roh jahat dalam kepercayaan Meitei.
claims.quote: It is considered as one of the Lai Phattaba beings or the evil spirits in traditional Meitei beliefs.

claims.statement: Some tales describe transformation when an animal passes over an unattended corpse.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian cerita menyebut transformasi terjadi saat hewan melewati mayat yang tidak dijaga.
claims.quote: Some stories describe the transformation as occurring when a dead body remains unattended and certain events—such as an animal, especially black cat, passing over the corpse—take place.

claims.statement: The being is said to resemble the deceased.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu dikatakan menyerupai orang yang meninggal.
claims.quote: The transformed being is often said to appear in the likeness of the deceased person.

claims.statement: In one tale an abandoned woman dies and transforms after a cat jumps over her corpse.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu cerita, seorang perempuan yang ditinggalkan meninggal dan berubah setelah kucing melompati mayatnya.
claims.quote: According to the folktale, a cat jumps over the corpse, triggering her transformation into a Hiyangthau.

claims.statement: When her husband returns, the being answers in his wife's voice and invites him inside.
claims.statement_id: Saat suaminya kembali, makhluk itu menjawab dengan suara istrinya dan mengundangnya masuk.
claims.quote: When he calls for his wife, the Hiyangthau responds using her voice and invites him inside.

claims.statement: In this folktale a woman became seriously ill and died without anyone knowing; her dead body lay in the house, a cat jumped over the body, and she turned into Hiyanthau.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, seorang perempuan jatuh sakit parah dan meninggal tanpa ada yang tahu; mayatnya tergeletak di rumah, seekor kucing melompati tubuhnya, dan ia berubah menjadi Hiyanthau.
claims.quote: The woman became seriously ill and died. No one knew she was dead. Her dead body lied in the house. A cat jumped over body and she turned into Hiyanthau.

claims.statement: In this folktale, when the husband returned and called, Hiyanthau replied in the form of the wife and told him to come in; she wore dishevelled clothes and her hair was rough as it had not been combed for days.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, ketika sang suami pulang dan memanggil, Hiyanthau menjawab dalam wujud istrinya dan menyuruhnya masuk; ia berpakaian kusut dan berambut kasar karena berhari-hari tidak disisir.
claims.quote: 'It is open. Just come in,' replied Hiyanthau in the form of the wife. The husband pushed the door open and came in. The wife was in dishevelled cloths. Her hair was rough as it had not been combed for days.

claims.statement: In this folktale the husband noticed his wife's broken body and trembled in fear; the wife looked at him with big round eyes and showed him her enormous teeth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, sang suami melihat tubuh istrinya yang rusak dan gemetar ketakutan; sang istri menatapnya dengan mata bulat besar dan memperlihatkan giginya yang sangat besar.
claims.quote: Then he noticed the broken body of his wife and trembled in fear. The wife looked at him with big round eyes and showed him her enormous teeth.

claims.statement: In this folktale the husband climbed up a liana; Hiyanthau came after him but could not touch the liana, so she threw stones at him and then sat down and waited for him to come down.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, sang suami memanjat sulur liana; Hiyanthau mengejarnya tetapi tidak dapat menyentuh liana itu sehingga ia melempar batu lalu duduk menunggu sang suami turun.
claims.quote: So ran and climbed up a liana. Hiyanthau came after him. She could not the touch the liana so she threw stone at him. Then sat down and waited for him to come down.

claims.statement: In this folktale, as the birds started chirping toward morning, Hiyanthau had to go back to the house and turned into a corpse.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, ketika burung-burung mulai berkicau menjelang pagi, Hiyanthau harus kembali ke rumah dan berubah menjadi mayat.
claims.quote: The birds started chirping as the morning time approached. Hiyanthau had to go back to the house, and she turned into a corpse.

claims.statement: In this folktale a man who knew all about spirits and ghosts said she had turned into Hiyanthau and must be cremated at once with the necessary ceremonies; otherwise at night she would become alive again and torment the entire village.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, seorang yang paham tentang roh dan hantu menyatakan bahwa perempuan itu telah menjadi Hiyanthau dan harus segera dikremasi dengan upacara yang semestinya; jika tidak, pada malam hari ia akan hidup lagi dan menyiksa seluruh desa.
claims.quote: A knowledgeable man among them who knew all about spirits and ghost told them that she had turned into Hiyanthau. 'Without losing any time she must be cremated with all the necessary ceremonies. Otherwise, at night she will become alive again and torment the entire village,

claims.statement: Hiyang Athouba is a figure in Meitei mythology and folklore of ancient Kangleipak (early Manipur).
claims.statement_id: Hiyang Athouba adalah sosok dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di Kangleipak kuno (Manipur awal).
claims.quote: is a figure in Meitei mythology and folklore of ancient Kangleipak (early Manipur).

claims.statement: Jarita is a female Sarngika bird whose story appears in the Mahabharata.
claims.statement_id: Jarita adalah burung betina Sarngika yang kisahnya terdapat dalam Mahabharata.
claims.quote: Jarita (Sanskrit: जरित, IAST Jaritā) was a certain female bird of the species called Sarngika, whose story is told in the Mahabharata.

claims.statement: Mandapala takes the form of a male bird and has four sons with her.
claims.statement_id: Mandapala mengambil bentuk burung jantan dan memiliki empat anak dengannya.
claims.quote: The saint Mandapala, who returned from the shades because he had no son, assumed the form of a male bird, and by her had four sons.

claims.statement: Mandapala later abandons her.
claims.statement_id: Mandapala kemudian meninggalkannya.
claims.quote: The saint Mandapala, who returned from the shades because he had no son, assumed the form of a male bird, and by her had four sons. He then abandoned her.

claims.statement: She strives to protect her young when the Khandava Forest burns.
claims.statement_id: Ia berusaha melindungi anak-anaknya ketika Hutan Khandava terbakar.
claims.quote: In the conflagration of the Khandava Forest she showed great devotion to the protection of her children

claims.statement: Her young are saved through Mandapala's influence over the fire god.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anaknya diselamatkan melalui pengaruh Mandapala atas dewa api.
claims.quote: they were eventually saved through the influence of Mandapala over the god of fire.

claims.statement: In this text the Rishi, assuming the form of a Sarngaka, had connection with a female bird of the same species called Jarita and begat upon her four sons who were all reciters of the Vedas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, sang Resi berwujud burung Sarngaka dan berhubungan dengan seekor burung betina sejenis bernama Jarita, dan dari Jarita lahir empat putra yang semuanya pelafal Weda.
claims.quote: Assuming the form of a Sarngaka the Rishi had connection with a female bird of the same species called by the name of Jarita. And he begat upon her four sons who were all reciters of the Vedas.

claims.statement: The ascetic left his sons with their mother in that forest while they were still in eggs and went to another wife called Lapita.
claims.statement_id: Sang petapa meninggalkan putra-putranya bersama ibu mereka di hutan itu ketika masih berada dalam telur, lalu pergi kepada istri lain bernama Lapita.
claims.quote: Leaving all those sons of his with their mother in that forest, while they were still within eggs, the ascetic went to (another wife called by the name of) Lapita.

claims.statement: Moved by parental affection, Jarita brought up the children born of her, herself following the pursuits proper to her own species.
claims.statement_id: Digerakkan kasih sayang orang tua, Jarita membesarkan anak-anak yang lahir darinya sambil menjalani cara hidup yang wajar bagi jenisnya sendiri.
claims.quote: Moved by parental affection, she brought up these children born of her, herself following the pursuits proper to her own species.

claims.statement: Praised by Mandapala, Agni was gratified and asked what he could do; Mandapala with joined palms asked Agni to spare his children while burning the forest of Khandava.
claims.statement_id: Setelah dipuji Mandapala, Agni senang dan bertanya apa yang dapat ia lakukan; Mandapala dengan tangan terkatup memohon kepada Agni agar, ketika membakar hutan Khandava, anak-anaknya dibiarkan hidup.
claims.quote: thus praised by Mandapala, Agni was gratified with that Rishi of immeasurable energy; and the god, well-pleased, replied, 'What good can I do to thee?' Then Mandapala with joined palms said unto the carrier of clarified butter, 'While thou burnest the forest of Khandava, spare my children.'

claims.statement: In this text, for that reason he did not blaze forth to destroy Mandapala's children while consuming the forest of Khandava.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks ini, karena itulah ia tidak berkobar untuk membinasakan anak-anak Mandapala ketika melahap hutan Khandava.
claims.quote: It was, therefore, O monarch, that he blazed not forth, while consuming the forest of Khandava, for the destruction of Mandapala's children.

claims.statement: Their helpless mother Jarita, knowing the infants were too young to escape, was filled with sorrow and wept aloud.
claims.statement_id: Ketika api berkobar, Jarita, ibu mereka yang tak berdaya, tahu anak-anaknya terlalu kecil untuk melarikan diri, sangat sedih dan menangis keras.
claims.quote: Their mother, the helpless Jarita, knowing that they were too young to escape, was filled with sorrow and wept aloud.

claims.statement: In her lament Jarita says she sees no way of escape for the infants and will cover them with her wings and die with them.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ratapannya Jarita mengatakan ia tidak melihat jalan keluar bagi anak-anaknya dan akan menutupi mereka dengan sayapnya serta mati bersama mereka.
claims.quote: I do not, even by reflection, see any way of escape for you. I shall even cover you with my wings and die with you.

claims.statement: Jarita proposes that the infants enter a mouse's hole in the ground near the tree to escape the fire.
claims.statement_id: Jarita mengusulkan agar anak-anaknya masuk ke lubang tikus di dekat pohon itu untuk menghindari api.
claims.quote: Hearing what the infants said. Jarita replied, 'There is a hole here in the ground near to this tree, belonging to a mouse.

claims.statement: In her lament Jarita recalls the words of their father: Jaritari, the eldest, will be the support of the race; Sarisrikka will beget progeny; Stamvamitra will be devoted to asceticism; and Drona, the youngest, will become the foremost of those acquainted with the Vedas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ratapannya Jarita mengenang kata-kata ayah mereka: Jaritari, putra sulung, akan menjadi sandaran garis keturunan; Sarisrikka akan melahirkan keturunan; Stamvamitra akan mengabdi pada pertapaan; dan Drona, si bungsu, akan menjadi yang terdepan di antara para ahli Weda.
claims.quote: Upon this Jaritari, because he is the eldest of my sons, will my race depend. My second Sarisrikka will beget progeny for the expansion of my ancestors' race. My third, Stamvamitra, will be devoted to asceticism, and my youngest, Drona, will become the foremost of those acquainted with the Vedas.

claims.statement: The Khoirentak tiger is a monstrous tiger in Meitei mythology eventually killed by Khuman Khamba.
claims.statement_id: Khoirentak tiger adalah harimau mengerikan dalam mitologi Meitei yang akhirnya dibunuh Khuman Khamba.
claims.quote:
The Khoirentak tiger (Meitei: ꯈꯣꯢꯔꯦꯟꯇꯥꯛ ꯀꯤ ꯀꯩꯔꯦꯜ) was a vicious monster in Meitei mythology that lived in Khoirentak. It was eventually killed by Khuman Khamba.
The tiger caused havoc to the people of the Khoirentak in Ancient Moirang, thereby becoming the "man eater" of the region. Finally, Khuman Khamba and Nongban were ordered by the king, to catch the beast.

claims.statement: The tiger is known as a man-eater in the Khoirentak area.
claims.statement_id: Harimau itu dikenal sebagai pemangsa manusia di daerah Khoirentak.
claims.quote: The tiger caused havoc to the people of the Khoirentak in Ancient Moirang, thereby becoming the "man eater" of the region.

claims.statement: It lives in the forests and attacks villagers.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di hutan dan menyerang penduduk desa.
claims.quote: The tiger lived in the forests of the Khoirentak region and attacked villagers. It became a serious threat to the people and was responsible for several deaths. The events related to the tiger later became part of a major conflict involving royal figures of Moirang.

claims.statement: One victim is Kumja Lembi, sent by her stepmother to collect herbs in the forest.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu korbannya adalah Kumja Lembi yang dikirim ibu tirinya mencari tanaman di hutan.
claims.quote: One notable victim was Kumja Lembi, also known as Kumcha Lempi. She was a poor girl who lived with her stepmother and father. Her father was often away from home because of work. Her stepmother sent her to the forest to collect herbs. During this task, she was killed by the tiger.

claims.statement: Angom Nongban Kongyamba dies of wounds caused by the tiger.
claims.statement_id: Angom Nongban Kongyamba meninggal akibat luka yang disebabkan harimau.
claims.quote: Another victim was Angom Nongban Kongyamba, who was seriously injured by the tiger during the later events. He later died from these injuries.

claims.statement: During the court discussion an old man from the Phubala region told the king about the dangerous tiger threatening the people of Khoirentak; the king then changed his decision and announced that whoever killed the tiger would marry Princess Thoibi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sidang istana, seorang lelaki tua dari wilayah Phubala memberi tahu raja tentang harimau berbahaya yang mengancam rakyat Khoirentak; raja lalu mengubah keputusannya dan menyatakan bahwa siapa yang membunuh harimau itu akan menikahi Putri Thoibi.
claims.quote: During the court discussion, an old man from the Phubala region informed the king about the dangerous tiger threatening the people of Khoirentak. After hearing this, the king changed his decision. He declared that killing the tiger would decide the matter. He announced that whoever killed the tiger would marry Princess Thoibi.

claims.statement: When they found the tiger both threw their spears but the tiger avoided them; the tiger then attacked Kongyamba and bit him, causing his death.
claims.statement_id: Ketika menemukan harimau itu, keduanya melempar tombak tetapi harimau menghindarinya; harimau lalu menyerang Kongyamba dan menggigitnya hingga tewas.
claims.quote: When they found the tiger, both threw their spears, but the tiger avoided them. The tiger then attacked Kongyamba and bit him, causing his death.

claims.statement: Khamba went back; the tiger was hiding in the bushes but was visible from the king's stadium, jumped at Khamba, and Khamba struck it in the jaws with his spear and finally killed it.
claims.statement_id: Khamba kembali ke hutan; harimau bersembunyi di semak-semak tetapi terlihat dari stadion raja, lalu melompat ke arah Khamba, dan Khamba menusuk rahangnya dengan tombak hingga akhirnya membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Khamba went back. The tiger was hiding in the bushes but was visible from the king's stadium. The tiger jumped at Khamba. Khamba struck the tiger in its jaws with his spear and finally killed it.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, an old woman tells the King there is a tiger in the nearby jungle that they fear, and the King promises the Princess Thoibi to whoever kills the tiger.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, seorang perempuan tua berkata kepada Raja bahwa ada harimau di hutan dekat situ yang mereka takuti, dan Raja berjanji akan memberikan Putri Thoibi kepada siapa pun yang membunuh harimau itu.
claims.quote: an old woman came forth and said, “ My Lord King, there is a tiger in the jungle hard-by that we fear,” and the King said, “Let the tiger bear witness herein. Unto him that kills the tiger, will I give the Princess Thoibi.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, in the beast's lair they found the body of a girl but newly killed; the tiger turned away the thrown spears and bit Kongyamba so that he died, and Khamba wounded the beast and drove it off.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, di sarang binatang itu mereka menemukan mayat seorang gadis yang baru dibunuh; harimau menepis tombak yang dilemparkan, menggigit Kongyamba hingga tewas, dan Khamba melukainya lalu mengusirnya.
claims.quote: So they went and sought the lair of the beast, and in it they found the body of a girl but newly killed. Then they found the tiger, and sought to spear it, but it turned the spears away as they threw them. Then the tiger sprang upon them and bit Kongyamba so that he died, but Khamba wounded the beast, and drove it off.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, Khamba entered the jungle once more and found the tiger crouching in a hollow, half hidden by the jungle but in full view of the King's machan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba kembali ke hutan dan menemukan harimau meringkuk di lekukan tanah, setengah tersembunyi oleh semak tetapi terlihat penuh dari panggung Raja.
claims.quote: Then Khamba entered the jungle once more and found the tiger crouching in a hollow half hidden by the jungle, but in full view of the machan of the King.

claims.statement: In this summary of the epic, the tiger died as it fell; the King then gave rich gifts, wide lands, rights of fishery and robes of honour.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, harimau itu mati saat jatuh; Raja kemudian memberikan hadiah kaya, tanah luas, hak perikanan, dan jubah kehormatan.
claims.quote: the ravening jaws, so that it died as it fell. Then the King gave rich gifts to Kliamba, and bestowed upon him wide lands and rights of fishery, robes of honour,

claims.statement: Misshaku Kongo is Guhyapada, a Buddhist guardian carrying a vajra and baring his teeth.
claims.statement_id: Misshaku Kongo adalah Guhyapada, penjaga Buddhis yang membawa vajra dan menampakkan gigi.
claims.quote: Japanese: Misshaku Kongō; Korean: Miljeok geumgang; Vietnamese: Mật tích kim cương ) is a symbol of overt violence: he wields a vajra mallet "vajra-pāṇi" (a diamond club, thunderbolt stick, or sun symbol) and bares his teeth.

claims.statement: His mouth opens to form the ha or ah sound.
claims.statement_id: Mulutnya terbuka untuk bunyi ha atau ah.
claims.quote: His mouth is depicted as being in the shape necessary to form the "ha" or "ah" sound.

claims.statement: In Japan he is also called Agyo because of his open mouth.
claims.statement_id: Di Jepang ia juga disebut Agyo karena bentuk mulut terbuka.
claims.quote: Similarly, he is also known as Agyō (阿形, "a"-form, general term open-mouthed statues in aum pair) in Japan due to this detail as well.

claims.statement: Guhyapada and Narayana are considered manifestations of Vajrapani.
claims.statement_id: Guhyapada dan Narayana dianggap sebagai manifestasi Vajrapani.
claims.quote: Both Guhyapāda and Nārāyaṇa are seen as manifestations of Vajrapāni (Traditional Chinese: 執金剛神; simplified Chinese: 执金刚神; pinyin: Zhíjīngāng shén; Japanese: Shūkongōshin; Korean: Jip geumgang sin; Vietnamese: Chấp kim cang thần), with the name literally meaning "vajra-wielding god".

claims.statement: The Zhu tian zhuan names the guardian Miji who vows to remain near Buddha.
claims.statement_id: Teks Zhu tian zhuan menyebut penjaga bernama Miji yang berikrar selalu berada dekat Buddha.
claims.quote: 宝积经云。法意太子愿作力士。立名密迹。常亲近佛。在外威仪。省知如来一切密迹秘要之事。信乐不疑。

claims.statement: In Chinese Buddhism, Guhyapāda is regarded as one of the Twenty-Four Protective Deities, a grouping of dharmapalas often enshrined in the Daxiong of temples and monasteries.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme Tiongkok, Guhyapāda dianggap salah satu dari Dua Puluh Empat Dewa Pelindung, kelompok dharmapala yang sering dipuja di Daxiong kuil dan biara.
claims.quote: In Chinese Buddhism, Guhyapāda is regarded as one of the Twenty-Four Protective Deities, who are a grouping of dharmapalas often enshrined in the Daxiong of temples and monasteries.

claims.statement: In China he is also known as General Ha (哈将 Hā Jiāng), in reference to this iconographic detail.
claims.statement_id: Di Tiongkok ia juga dikenal sebagai Jenderal Ha (哈将 Hā Jiāng), merujuk pada ciri ikonografis mulut yang membentuk bunyi 'ha'.
claims.quote: In China, he is also known as General Ha (哈将 Hā Jiāng) in reference to this iconographic detail.

claims.statement: According to the Zhu tian zhuan, the figure of Miji is shown with bared torso, glaring eyes and open mouth, a red body, a topknot on the head, a pestle (chu) in hand and bare feet, and is majestic and valiant.
claims.statement_id: Menurut 重編諸天傳, rupa Mijī digambarkan bertelanjang dada, bermata melotot dan mulut terbuka, seluruh tubuh merah, berambut disanggul di kepala, memegang tongkat (chu) di tangan, berkaki telanjang, dan gagah perkasa.
claims.quote: 其像也。露袒其身。怒目开口。徧体赤色。头上有髻。手中执杵。以跣双足。威楞勇倢。

claims.statement: According to the Dīrghāgama as cited in the Zhu tian zhuan, when an adherent of another teaching would not answer, the Buddha said the strongman Miji, vajra bell and pestle in hand, was at his side and would split the man's head into seven parts; the strongman then appeared in the sky and the man believed and submitted.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan Dīrghāgama dalam 重編諸天傳, ketika seorang penganut ajaran lain enggan menjawab, Buddha mengatakan bahwa Mijī sang kesatria, dengan lonceng dan tongkat vajra di tangan, berada di sisinya dan akan memecah kepala orang itu menjadi tujuh bagian; sang kesatria lalu tampak di angkasa dan orang itu pun percaya dan tunduk.
claims.quote: 长阿含云。外道阿摩昼问佛四姓。佛云汝姓是释迦奴种。彼不肯信。故不答。佛云。汝宜速答。密迹力士手执金刚铃杵在吾左右。当破汝头分为七分。时力士即现空中。彼方信伏。

claims.statement: According to the Zhu tian zhuan, in the time of the First Emperor of Qin, eighteen monks from India, including Shilifang, who were imprisoned at Chang'an were freed when the vajra strongman broke the prison wall.
claims.statement_id: Menurut 重編諸天傳, pada zaman Kaisar Pertama Qin, delapan belas biksu dari India yang dipenjara di Chang'an, termasuk 室利房, dibebaskan ketika kesatria vajra menjebol tembok penjara.
claims.quote: 又秦始皇时。天竺室利房等沙门一十八人来至长安。始皇囚於狱中。金刚力士破狱垣以出之。

claims.statement: According to the Zhu tian zhuan citing the Golden Light text, Vajra Miji is a great king of spirits, and his retinue of five hundred are all great bodhisattvas.
claims.statement_id: Menurut 重編諸天傳 yang mengutip Sutra Cahaya Emas, Vajra Mijī adalah raja besar para roh, dan para pengikutnya yang berjumlah lima ratus semuanya adalah bodhisatwa besar.
claims.quote: 光明云。金刚密迹。大鬼神王。及其眷属五百徒党。一切皆是大菩萨等。

claims.statement: Nittaewo are small humanoids of Veddha mythology and Sri Lankan folklore.
claims.statement_id: Nittaewo adalah humanoid bertubuh kecil dalam mitologi Veddha dan cerita rakyat Sri Lanka.

claims.statement_id: Kangla sha adalah makhluk penjaga suci dalam mitologi Meitei, bertubuh singa dan berkepala naga bertanduk dua.
claims.quote:
In Meitei mythology and Sanamahism, the  indigenous religion of Manipur, Kanglā shā (Meitei: ꯀꯡꯂꯥ ꯁꯥ, lit. 'beast of the Kangla') is a sacred guardian beast with a lion's body and a two-horned dragon's head.
It is a royal symbol of the Meitei royalties (Ningthouja dynasty).
The most remarkable statues dedicated to "Kangla Sa" stand inside the Kangla.

claims.statement: The creature is a Meitei royal symbol.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu merupakan lambang kerajaan Meitei.
claims.quote: It is a royal symbol of the Meitei royalties (Ningthouja dynasty).

claims.statement: Traditional race winners are declared after symbolically touching its statue.
claims.statement_id: Pemenang perlombaan tradisional ditentukan setelah menyentuh patungnya secara simbolis.
claims.quote: In Meitei traditional race competitions, winners of the race are declared only after symbolically touching the statue of the dragon "Kangla Sha".

claims.statement: Raja Nara Singh reconstructs two Kangla Sha statues in 1844.
claims.statement_id: Raja Nara Singh membangun kembali dua patung Kangla Sha pada 1844.
claims.quote: During the months of June and July in the year 1844, Meitei king Raja Nara Singh (Meitei: ꯅꯤꯡꯊꯧ ꯅꯔꯁꯤꯡꯍ) reconstructed the two statues of the Kangla Sha dragons once again.

claims.statement: British troops destroy the two statues with artillery fire on 20 July 1891.
claims.statement_id: Pasukan Inggris menghancurkan dua patung itu dengan tembakan artileri pada 20 Juli 1891.
claims.quote: During the British conquest of the Anglo Manipur War of 1891, the British forces led by Captain Allen demolished the two statues of the Kangla Sha dragons by blasting them by artillery fire into pieces on 20 July 1891.

claims.statement: Khyah are humanoid creatures of Newar folklore, portrayed as short, fat, hairy and apelike.
claims.statement_id: Khyah adalah makhluk humanoid dalam cerita rakyat Newar, digambarkan pendek, gemuk, berbulu, dan mirip kera.
claims.quote: Khyāh (Newar: 𑐏𑑂𑐫𑐵𑑅; alternative spellings Khyā or Khyāk) is a mythical humanoid creature in Newari folklore. It is depicted as a fat, hairy and short ape-like creature.

claims.statement: Friendly khyah bring goodness, while bad ones bring trouble.
claims.statement_id: Khyah yang bersahabat membawa kebaikan, sedangkan yang jahat membawa masalah.
claims.quote: Khyahs appear in children's stories popular in Newar society. A friendly Khyah fills the home with goodness while bad ones bring trouble. A white Khyah is believed to bring good luck while a black one can create problems. Encountering a Khyah can make one ill. Khyahs are said to tickle their victims to death.

claims.statement: In Newar culture they attend Lakshmi and guard bags of coins in depictions.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebudayaan Newar mereka mendampingi Lakshmi dan menjaga kantong uang dalam penggambarannya.
claims.quote: In Newar culture, Khyahs attend to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, and pictures of the deity show them guarding overflowing bags of coins. Household Khyahs usually dwell in the attic and dark storerooms. They are said to fear electric lighting.

claims.statement: Household khyah dwell in attics and dark storerooms.
claims.statement_id: Khyah rumah tinggal di loteng dan ruang penyimpanan gelap.
claims.quote: Household Khyahs usually dwell in the attic and dark storerooms. They are said to fear electric lighting.

claims.statement: Khyah and Kawancha appear in sacred dance dramas and as temple guardians.
claims.statement_id: Khyah dan Kawancha muncul dalam drama tari suci dan menjadi penjaga kuil.
claims.quote: The antithesis of the Khyah is the Kawanchā, a skeleton. Khyahs and Kawanchas appear as supporting characters in sacred dance dramas of the Newars. Images of Khyahs and Kawanchas are also placed at temples as guardians of the shrine.

claims.statement: Khyah Pyakhan dances at the Yenya festival feature actors in khyah costumes.
claims.statement_id: Tari Khyah Pyakhan pada festival Yenya menampilkan aktor berkostum Khyah.
claims.quote: During the Yenya festival in Kathmandu, dance performances are held at market squares and the Durbar Square where actors dressed in Khyah costumes give dance performances. The dances, known as Khyāh Pyākhan (ख्याः प्याखं), consist of antics and tumbling.

claims.statement: Kichkandi is a woman's spirit in Nepalese folklore attached to an uncremated part of her body.
claims.statement_id: Kichkandi adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Nepal yang melekat pada bagian tubuhnya yang belum dikremasi.
claims.quote: In Nepalese folklore or mythology, kichkanya (Nepali: किच्कन्या) also referred to as Kichkandi (Nepali: किच्कन्डी) is a spirit of a woman that is latched to an uncremated part of her dead body, usually a bone.

claims.statement: Tales place her at the site of an untimely death.
claims.statement_id: Cerita menempatkannya di lokasi kematian yang tidak wajar.
claims.quote: Children often grow up hearing the stories of such tortured souls of women who wander the site of their untimely death.

claims.statement: She is said to have long black hair, a pale complexion and red bridal clothing.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan berambut panjang hitam, berkulit pucat, dan memakai pakaian pengantin merah.
claims.quote: they are supposed to have unusually long black hair, pale and bony complexion and dressed up in a red bridal dress.

claims.statement: Her feet are said to face backward.
claims.statement_id: Kakinya dikatakan menghadap ke belakang.
claims.quote: It is said that they can be identified by looking at their feet, which face backward.

claims.statement: She lures a solitary male traveller and drains his life force.
claims.statement_id: Ia memikat pelancong laki-laki sendirian dan menyerap daya hidupnya.
claims.quote: People usually describe them as alluring and young female, who lures a lonely male traveler and saps their life force. The victims are said to turn out drained of their life and skinny. According to other tales told by locals and cab drivers, these spirits are also known to hitchhike late at night.

claims.quote: In Bhoot Police, a 2021 Bollywood film, the tea estate of the character Maya(played by Yami Gautam) is haunted by a kichkandi.
